section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which agency handles driver licensing and permits in Missouri?
options: a:Missouri DMV,b:Missouri Department of Revenue (DOR),c:Missouri DOT,d:Missouri Secretary of State
note: Missouri's Department of Revenue (DOR) handles driver licensing, vehicle registration, and permits. Missouri does not have a traditional DMV — if you need a permit or license, visit a Missouri DOR license office.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age to apply for a Missouri learner's permit?
options: a:14,b:15,c:16,d:15 and a half
note: Missouri allows teens to apply for a learner's permit (Temporary Instruction Permit or TIPIC) at age 15. The permit allows supervised driving practice as the first step in Missouri's GDL program.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Missouri's real DOR knowledge test has 25 questions. How many must you answer correctly to pass?
note: Missouri's DOR knowledge test requires 20 correct answers out of 25 — an 80% passing threshold. You can miss up to 5 questions. Missing 6 or more means you fail and must wait before retaking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a Missouri driver age 21 or older?
note: Missouri sets the DWI (Driving While Intoxicated) limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Missouri also has a separate EWID (Excessive BAC) charge for 0.15% or higher, carrying enhanced penalties. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What BAC triggers Missouri's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21?
note: Missouri sets the underage alcohol limit at 0.02% BAC for drivers under 21. This is effectively zero tolerance — any detectable amount above 0.02% is illegal for underage drivers in Missouri.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Missouri's GDL program, how many hours of supervised driving must a permit holder complete?
options: a:20 hours (2 at night),b:30 hours (no night requirement),c:40 hours (10 at night),d:50 hours (no night requirement)
note: Missouri requires 40 hours of supervised driving practice, with at least 10 hours driven at night. The supervising driver must be a licensed driver age 21 or older seated in the front seat. These hours must be logged and certified before applying for an intermediate driver's license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on Missouri urban streets when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:45 mph
note: Missouri sets the default speed limit in any city, town, or village (urban districts) at 25 mph when no sign is posted. Rural highways are set at 60 mph unless posted otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is Missouri's default speed limit on rural highways when no sign is posted?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: Missouri's default speed limit on rural roads and highways is 60 mph — slightly higher than the 55 mph default used by many other states. This reflects Missouri's flatter terrain and wider rural roads in many areas. Always check for posted signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Missouri's Move Over law requires what when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle with flashing lights on a highway?
options: a:Slow to 20 mph only,b:Move one lane away if safe, or reduce speed if a lane change is not possible,c:Stop completely behind the vehicle,d:Only required for police — not tow trucks
note: Missouri's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from stationary emergency, law enforcement, utility, or tow vehicles with flashing lights. If a safe lane change is not possible, significantly reduce speed. The law applies to all such vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You approach a school bus stopped on an undivided road with flashing red lights. What must you do?
options: a:Stop only if you are behind the bus,b:Stop in both directions at least 20 feet from the bus,c:Slow to 15 mph and proceed carefully,d:Stop only if children are visible
note: Missouri law requires all vehicles in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights. Wait until the stop arm retracts and lights stop before proceeding. On a divided highway, only traffic behind the bus must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must Missouri drivers turn on their headlights?
options: a:Only from sunset to sunrise,b:From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and when visibility is under 500 feet,c:Only in rain and fog,d:Only after 9 PM
note: Missouri requires headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and whenever weather or conditions reduce visibility to less than 500 feet. This includes rain, fog, snow, and other conditions reducing visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Yield to cross traffic and proceed,c:Come to a complete stop, yield to all traffic, and proceed when safe,d:Continue at the posted speed
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign in Missouri. Make a complete stop, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe. A flashing yellow requires caution but not a complete stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum recommended following distance in Missouri under normal conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Missouri recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. In rain, fog, or on wet roads, increase to at least 6 seconds. The 3-second rule provides the minimum reaction time to stop safely if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane road in Missouri, when may you legally cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:When the road ahead is visible for at least 500 feet,b:You may never cross a solid yellow line on your side to pass,c:When the vehicle ahead is going well below the speed limit,d:When you signal for at least 200 feet first
note: A solid yellow line on your side prohibits crossing the center line to pass. No exceptions. Only when a broken (dashed) yellow line is on your side may you pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Missouri seatbelt law requires which vehicle occupants to wear a seatbelt?
options: a:Driver and front-seat passengers only,b:All occupants in the front seat,c:All occupants,d:Only those under 18
note: Missouri requires all vehicle occupants — in all seating positions — to wear a seatbelt. Missouri has primary enforcement. Children must use appropriate child safety seats based on age and size. Violations carry fines.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches from behind, you must:
options: a:Speed up and exit the roadway,b:Pull to the right edge and stop,c:Slow to 10 mph in your lane,d:Move to the center of the road
note: Missouri law requires you to immediately pull to the right edge of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches. Remain stopped until the vehicle has passed. If in an intersection, clear it first, then pull to the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can you make a right turn on a red light in Missouri?
options: a:No, right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:Yes, after a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Yes, without stopping if the turn is clear,d:Only on one-way streets
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Missouri after a complete stop, yielding to all pedestrians and cross traffic, and unless a 'No Turn on Red' sign is posted. Always make a full stop — rolling through on red while turning right is illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on Missouri rural interstate highways?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: Missouri's maximum speed limit on rural interstate highways is 70 mph for passenger vehicles. Urban sections may have lower posted limits. Always check posted signs — 70 mph is the ceiling, not a universal default.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian is crossing in a marked crosswalk. You must:
options: a:Proceed if you have a green light,b:Slow to 15 mph and proceed carefully,c:Stop and yield until the pedestrian has completely crossed the roadway,d:Yield only if the pedestrian is in your direct lane
note: Missouri law requires stopping and yielding to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. You must remain stopped until the pedestrian has completely crossed — even with a green light. Pedestrian right-of-way in a crosswalk is absolute.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the shape and color of a standard warning sign in Missouri?
options: a:Rectangle, white,b:Octagon, red,c:Diamond, yellow,d:Triangle, orange
note: Warning signs are yellow diamond-shaped signs used nationwide. They alert drivers to potential hazards such as curves, merging lanes, school zones, and railroad crossings. The diamond shape and yellow color together indicate extra caution is needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Missouri law requires drivers to signal before turning or changing lanes at least how far in advance?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet,d:300 feet
note: Missouri law requires signaling at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. On higher-speed roads, earlier signaling is advisable. Failing to signal or signaling too late is illegal and potentially dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Missouri, what is the consequence of refusing a chemical test after being lawfully stopped for DWI?
options: a:No penalty — refusal is a protected right,b:Automatic 1-year license revocation for a first refusal,c:Only a minor fine,d:License loss only if convicted of DWI
note: Missouri's implied consent law means refusing a chemical test after a DWI stop results in a 1-year license revocation for a first offense. The refusal itself carries this penalty, separate from any DWI conviction. Refusal can also be used as evidence against you in court.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in fog in Missouri, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beams for maximum visibility,b:Low beams or fog lights,c:Hazard flashers only,d:No lights — they reflect off fog
note: In fog, use low beams or dedicated fog lights. High beams reflect off fog particles and create blinding glare. Missouri's Mississippi River valley areas can experience frequent river fog — especially in the morning — making this rule particularly important in those regions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Missouri's DOR issues a Temporary Instruction Permit (TIPIC) for new drivers. What does TIPIC stand for and what is it used for?
options: a:Temporary Internal Permit for Individual Certification — used for commercial licenses,b:Temporary Instruction Permit Identification Card — used as the learner's permit for supervised driving practice,c:Temporary Interstate Permission and Insurance Card — used for out-of-state driving,d:Transportation Identity Permit for In-County driving — limited to local roads only
note: Missouri's Temporary Instruction Permit Identification Card (TIPIC) is the official learner's permit issued to new drivers age 15 and older. It allows supervised driving practice and must be carried while driving. The TIPIC is the first step in Missouri's GDL program, before advancing to an intermediate driver's license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a vehicle to your right. Who goes first?
options: a:You do — you were both there simultaneously,b:The vehicle on your right has the right of way,c:Whoever is going straight has priority,d:The vehicle turning right always goes first
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a 4-way stop, yield to the vehicle on the right. This is the universal tie-breaking rule at all-way stops. If you arrived clearly first, you proceed first regardless of direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, who must yield?
options: a:The public traffic must always stop for you.,b:You may force your way into traffic if necessary.,c:The driver entering from the driveway should yield to traffic already on the public road.
note: A driver entering a public road from a driveway, alley, or private road must yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians already on the public roadway. You may only enter when there is a safe gap so that other road users do not have to slow or stop suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you proceed when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Drive carefully through the intersection after slowing and scanning for hazards.,b:Stop and wait for the light to change.,c:Make a U-turn because the road is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed with extra caution. Look left, right, and ahead for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards before entering the intersection.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside and do not tailgate them.,b:Never pass them under any circumstances.,c:Flash your lights at them.
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots directly behind them, along both sides, and close in front. To stay visible, avoid driving right beside them for long periods and never follow too closely. If you cannot see the driver’s mirrors, they likely cannot see you.

question: When it begins to rain while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and turn on your headlights.,b:Drive at the posted maximum speed limit.,c:Speed up to get through the rain quickly.
note: When it starts to rain, roads become especially slippery and visibility drops. You should slow down, increase following distance, and turn on your headlights so you can see and be seen. If visibility becomes very poor, pull off the road safely and wait for conditions to improve.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance.,b:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,c:Defending yourself by getting ahead of poor drivers.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road, spotting potential hazards early, and adjusting your speed or position to avoid conflicts and crashes. You leave space, expect mistakes from others, and act early to stay out of trouble.

question: If you are taking a non-prescription (over-the-counter) drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Ignore the label and drive as usual.,b:Only drive if you feel fine.,c:Mix it with alcohol to see how it affects you.,d:Read the label for warnings about driving.
note: Many over‑the‑counter medicines can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. Always read the label for warnings about driving or operating machinery, and if you are unsure how it will affect you, ask a doctor or pharmacist before driving.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It increases air pollution.,b:It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.,c:It may reduce engine performance.
note: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can let carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless poisonous gas, enter the passenger compartment. Breathing carbon monoxide can cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, and even death. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Only a BAC above the legal limit will impair concentration.,b:Alcohol does not limit concentration, perception, or memory.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol affect the brain and can reduce concentration, slow reaction time, and impair judgment and perception. You do not need to be above the legal BAC limit to be impaired; any drinking before driving increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is NOT permitted while stopped in a travel lane?
options: a:Stopping to drop off passengers.,b:Stopping to look up an address.,c:Keeping moving until you can safely pull off the road.
note: You should not stop and remain in a travel lane for non-emergency reasons because you create a hazard for traffic behind you. If you need to drop off passengers, check directions, or deal with a problem, continue driving until you can safely pull off the roadway and stop out of the flow of traffic.

question: If someone has been drinking, what will help them sober up quickly?
options: a:Hot coffee.,b:Fresh air.,c:Time—only the passage of time will lessen alcohol's effects.
note: Once alcohol is in your system, only time allows your body to break it down. Coffee, cold showers, fresh air, or exercise may make you feel more awake, but they do not reduce your blood alcohol concentration or make you safe to drive.

question: How does consuming alcohol while taking drugs affect you?
options: a:It reduces the effects of both.,b:It can increase the effects of both, making driving more dangerous.,c:It helps cure whatever illness you have.
note: Mixing alcohol with drugs—whether prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal—can greatly increase the effects of each. This combination can severely impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making driving extremely dangerous and unpredictable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle based on lane markings between lanes moving the same direction?
options: a:When the dividing line is a broken white line.,b:When there is a solid yellow line.,c:When there is a double solid yellow line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and you may cross them to change lanes or pass when it is safe. Solid or double solid yellow lines generally separate traffic moving in opposite directions and are not used to indicate passing between same‑direction lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as which sign?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A solid red light.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop just as you would at a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic or pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: When traveling to a place you don't know well, what should you do before you drive?
options: a:Only have a general idea where your destination is.,b:Plan your route ahead of time.,c:Rely solely on road signs to find your way.
note: Before driving to an unfamiliar place, plan your route in advance. Knowing your turns, exits, and main roads ahead of time reduces last‑second maneuvers, distractions, and the risk of getting lost.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed with caution without stopping.,b:Come to a complete stop, then go when safe.,c:Slow down but you don’t have to stop.
note: At a flashing red light you must come to a complete stop, just as at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic or pedestrians in or approaching the intersection, then proceed only when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When overtaking on a multilane highway, what should you do before beginning to pass?
options: a:Pass only on the right.,b:Watch for oncoming traffic.,c:Make sure the passing lane is clear and signal before changing lanes.
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, check that the lane you will move into is clear by using your mirrors and checking blind spots, then signal before changing lanes. This helps other drivers anticipate your movement and reduces the risk of a collision.

question: How does being distracted while driving usually affect your reactions to hazards?
options: a:It has no effect.,b:It generally slows your reaction to hazards.,c:It makes you react faster.
note: Distractions like texting, eating, or adjusting controls take your eyes, mind, or hands away from driving. This slows how quickly you notice and react to hazards, which greatly increases your chance of a crash.

question: Which situation most commonly causes “highway hypnosis” while driving?
options: a:Too much sleep the night before your trip.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods and failing to actively scan.
note: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning mirrors and the road. Your mind drifts, awareness drops, and you may not remember parts of the drive, which is very dangerous at highway speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and safely turn around.,b:Stop on the shoulder and back up to the exit.,c:Make an immediate U-turn across lanes.
note: If you miss your exit, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit. Never stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the interstate; those actions can cause serious high‑speed crashes.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Proceed when you think it is clear.,b:Turn up the radio to listen for trains.,c:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.,d:Always wait for a flagger even if none is present.
note: At a crossing with only a crossbuck, slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be ready to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Merging traffic is ahead.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Pedestrian crossing only.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield and react to other traffic, pedestrians, or unexpected hazards in the intersection.

question: What is the purpose of a diamond-shaped road sign?
options: a:To warn of existing or possible hazards.,b:To indicate a public recreation area.,c:To mark school zones.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert drivers to existing or potential hazards or changes in road conditions, such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or work zones. Recognizing this shape helps you prepare to slow down, change lanes, or take other precautions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a multi-lane street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane closest to your previous lane.,b:Into the middle lane regardless of approach.,c:Into any lane and then change immediately.
note: When you turn onto a multi-lane street, you must turn into the lane that is directly next to the one you came from. For example, if you turn left from the leftmost lane, you must enter the leftmost lane of the new road. This keeps traffic predictable and prevents conflicts with vehicles turning from other directions.

question: Which of these is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes.,b:Driving more slowly than normal traffic.,c:Making quick and sudden stops.
note: Weaving between lanes is a strong sign of possible impairment, but driving much slower than surrounding traffic and making quick, sudden stops are also common signs of a drunk or impaired driver. Any erratic or unusual driving behavior—such as drifting, inconsistent speed, delayed starts at green lights, or over‑braking—can indicate impairment and should make you increase your following distance and be prepared to avoid the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Go.,b:Yield to other cars.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before entering the intersection. You may proceed only if you are already so close that stopping safely is not possible without hard braking or risking a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may legally pass another vehicle when:
options: a:Your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.,b:On a hill or in a curve where visibility is limited.,c:The center line on your side of the roadway is a broken yellow line and it is safe to pass.,d:By driving onto the highway shoulder.
note: You may pass another vehicle only when the center line on your side is a broken yellow line and you have enough clear distance ahead to pass safely. Never pass on hills, curves, where your view is blocked, across solid yellow lines, or by driving onto the shoulder, because oncoming traffic or roadside hazards may not be visible in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are the minimum and maximum speed limits on Missouri interstates under normal conditions?
options: a:40 mph minimum and 70 mph maximum.,b:40 mph minimum and 55 mph maximum.,c:30 mph minimum and 70 mph maximum.
note: On Missouri interstate highways under normal conditions, the usual posted maximum speed is 70 mph and the minimum is 40 mph. Driving slower than the minimum can be unsafe because it disrupts traffic flow, and driving faster than the maximum is illegal and increases crash risk.

question: What does the abbreviation FACT stand for?
options: a:Failure to Appear in Court for Traffic violations.,b:Finance A Car Today.,c:Full Ambulance Cannot Turn.,d:Fear of Authority Causes Tension.
note: FACT stands for Failure to Appear in Court for Traffic violations. If you do not appear in court or pay required fines for a traffic ticket, the court can notify the licensing authority, which may result in suspension of your driving privilege until the matter is resolved.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do while driving on major highways to avoid highway hypnosis and be ready for hazards?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving.,b:Stay alert.,c:Be ready to react to road hazards.
note: To avoid highway hypnosis on major highways, you should keep your eyes moving, stay mentally alert, and be ready to react to hazards. Scan the road ahead, check your mirrors frequently, and avoid staring at any one spot for too long so you can spot problems early and respond safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car that sounds its horn first.,b:The car approaching from the right.,c:The car approaching from the left.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), you must yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right when you arrive at the same time. This rule helps drivers know who should proceed first and reduces confusion and collisions.

question: A double solid yellow centerline indicates what?
options: a:Single broken yellow.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Combination solid and broken yellow.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road, when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,b:May drive through the intersection if the way is clear.,c:Must slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed straight or turn if the intersection is clear, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left. Green never means you can go without checking for other road users.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach,b:The individual's body weight,c:The time between drinks,d:All of the above
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is affected by several factors, including how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and whether you have food in your stomach. Food can slow alcohol absorption but does not prevent impairment, so all of the listed factors play a role.

question: Where are roads most likely to freeze quickly?
options: a:In shaded areas such as those by trees or buildings.,b:On straight, open sections of road.,c:Where the sun hits directly.
note: Shaded areas such as those under trees, on bridges, or near buildings freeze sooner and stay icy longer because they receive less sunlight. Even when the rest of the road looks clear, these shaded spots can still be slippery and require extra caution.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, how should you return to the pavement?
options: a:Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop your car on the edge of the road.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually while keeping the vehicle under control. Once your speed is reduced and the way is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement; sudden braking or sharp steering can cause you to lose control.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather.,b:New drivers.,c:Human error.
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, such as inattention, following too closely, speeding, or misjudging gaps and speeds. While weather and road conditions matter, driver decisions and mistakes are the primary cause of most collisions.

question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles generally have what regarding blind spots?
options: a:Larger blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:No blind spots at all.
note: Larger vehicles like trucks and buses sit higher and have bigger areas around them that the driver cannot see in mirrors. These larger blind spots are along the sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. Because of this, you should avoid lingering next to or close behind large vehicles where the driver may not see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what is required?
options: a:You must temporarily use the lane for oncoming traffic and ensure it is safe and legal to pass.,b:You may not cross the centerline where passing is prohibited by signs or solid lines.,c:Flashing your headlights does not give you the right-of-way and should not be used to force oncoming traffic to yield.
note: On a typical two-lane, two-way road, you must move into the lane used by oncoming traffic to pass a slower vehicle. You may only do this where passing is legal (for example, with a broken centerline and no signs prohibiting passing) and when you have enough clear distance ahead to complete the pass safely without interfering with oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid double yellow line to pass, and never rely on flashing headlights to force others to move.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Cross the tracks at your own risk if you are in a hurry.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has passed completely.
note: If a train is close enough to be a danger, you must stop and wait until it has completely passed and the tracks are clear. Trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right-of-way. Never try to beat a train, drive around lowered gates, or cross when you are unsure if another train is coming.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Check your side-view mirror only.,b:Check your rearview mirror only.,c:Check side and rearview mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, first check your mirrors to see traffic behind and to the sides, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. This head check helps you see vehicles that mirrors may miss, such as cars or motorcycles in the next lane.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has blinding headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Look directly at the headlights until they dim.,b:Look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle has passed.,c:Flash your high beams to signal them to dim.
note: When an oncoming vehicle’s headlights are too bright, avoid looking directly at them. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide until the vehicle passes. This reduces glare and helps you maintain your lane position. Do not stare at the lights or flash your high beams, which can make the situation more dangerous for both drivers.

question: How should you respond when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution. It warns that there may be a hazard or cross traffic, but it does not require a full stop unless needed for safety.

question: When roads may be slippery, what should you avoid?
options: a:Using cruise control and making sudden speed or steering changes.,b:Reducing your speed.,c:Driving more cautiously than normal.
note: On slippery roads, you should avoid using cruise control and avoid any sudden changes in speed or steering. Instead, reduce your speed gradually and drive more smoothly to maintain traction and control.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Start driving and let emotions settle.,b:Take time to calm down and focus on driving before you start.,c:Drive faster to get it over with.
note: Strong emotions like anger, nervousness, or crying can distract you and slow your reactions. You should wait until you have calmed down and can focus fully on driving before you start the vehicle.

question: What does a red circle with a diagonal slash on a regulatory sign mean?
options: a:The indicated action is forbidden.,b:Drivers must come to a complete stop.,c:Some drivers should yield to others.
note: A red circle with a diagonal slash over a symbol means that the action shown is not allowed. For example, a right-turn arrow with this symbol means no right turn at that location.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind on an uphill grade, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted limit.,b:You may not be able to safely pass the truck because of limited visibility or grade.,c:The truck will always signal you to pass.
note: When you approach a heavy truck from behind on an uphill grade, you should expect it to be moving more slowly than the posted speed limit because large vehicles lose speed climbing hills. You must be prepared to slow down and follow at a safe distance, and only pass if you have clear visibility and enough space to do so safely and legally.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating them.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
note: If you encounter an aggressive driver, stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and do not engage. Safely slow down, create space, and let them pass when you can. This reduces the chance of a road-rage incident and keeps you in control of the situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.,b:Maintain normal speed without stopping.,c:Stop and wait for a police officer to direct you.
note: A green light allows you to turn, but it does not give you the right to ignore others. When turning right on green, you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any traffic already in or close to the intersection. Only complete the turn when it is safe and clear.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using its lights and/or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and stay in your lane.,b:Pull to the right curb and stop, yielding a clear path.,c:Keep driving in your lane and ignore it.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and/or siren, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop, allowing a clear path. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

question: What is required regarding visibility of license plates and plate frames in Missouri?
options: a:A frame may cover the word "Missouri" on the plate.,b:Plate frames must not cover any portion of the plate's numbers, letters, state name, or registration stickers.,c:A frame may cover the month and year registration stickers.
note: License plates must be clearly readable so officers and cameras can see the numbers, letters, state name, and registration stickers. Plate frames or covers cannot block or obscure any part of this information. If any wording, numbers, or stickers are covered, you can be cited.

question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Night driving.,b:High speeds.,c:Slow speeds.
note: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop and the more severe a crash will be. Stopping distance increases sharply with speed because both reaction distance and braking distance grow, and impact force rises with speed. Driving at high speeds greatly increases your risk.

question: If you are involved in a crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop at once.,b:Leave the scene if damage is only minor.,c:Only call the police if someone is injured.,d:Move injured people immediately without checking injuries.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop immediately. After stopping, protect the scene if you can do so safely, check for injuries, call emergency services if needed, and exchange information. Do not leave the scene, and do not move injured people unless there is immediate danger, such as fire or risk of another collision.

question: About how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph need to stop?
options: a:50 feet,b:125 feet,c:Up to 400 feet.
note: A fully loaded tractor‑trailer needs much more distance to stop than a passenger car. At about 55 mph, it can take roughly the length of a football field plus the end zones—up to about 400 feet—to come to a complete stop. This is why you should avoid cutting closely in front of large trucks and always allow them extra space.

question: What is the correct method for backing a vehicle?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing, not relying solely on mirrors.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Open your door and step out to check behind you.
note: When backing, first walk around and check behind your vehicle for children, objects, or other hazards. Then, while backing, turn your head and look directly through the rear window instead of relying only on mirrors. Back slowly and be prepared to stop if you lose sight of what is behind you.

question: On roads without sidewalks, which side should pedestrians walk on?
options: a:The side that faces oncoming traffic.,b:The same side that traffic travels on.,c:The side with lighter traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the side facing oncoming traffic. This allows them to see approaching vehicles and react if a driver drifts toward them. They should stay as far to the left as practical and be especially cautious in low‑visibility conditions.

question: If you arrive at your car feeling angry after an incident, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Play loud music so you won’t think about it.,b:Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin driving home.
note: Driving while angry or emotionally upset can lead to poor judgment, aggressive driving, and slower reaction times. If you reach your car feeling very upset, take a few minutes to calm down before driving. Use that time to breathe, sit quietly, or walk briefly so you are in control of your emotions when you start driving.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, you should:
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and continue driving.,b:Stop immediately where you are.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.,d:Pull over to the right and stop.
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed. In heavy traffic, continue to move carefully until you can pull right and create a clear path.

question: What primarily affects your ability to stop your vehicle safely?
options: a:The condition of the road and roadway surfaces.,b:The time of day.,c:Signal lights alone.
note: Stopping distance depends heavily on road surface and conditions. Wet, icy, or loose surfaces greatly increase how far it takes to stop, so you must slow down and increase following distance to stop safely.

question: When making a turn, how should you adjust your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Maintain the same speed as before.,c:Reduce or otherwise adjust your speed to maintain control.
note: Before and during a turn, you should slow to a safe speed so you can stay in your lane and keep control of the vehicle. Enter the turn at a speed that lets you react to hazards and avoid skidding.

question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Do not slow down until you have moved onto the exit ramp, then decelerate.,b:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.,c:Keep speed constant once on the exit ramp.
note: On freeways, stay at freeway speed until you are actually in the exit lane or on the exit ramp. Then use the deceleration lane or ramp to slow to the posted exit or curve speed, so you don’t disrupt fast traffic behind you.

question: How can you avoid having to make sudden emergency stops when driving in traffic?
options: a:Drive in the right lane only.,b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,c:Honk your horn to alert others of your presence.
note: To avoid sudden emergency stops, look well ahead in traffic and keep a safe following distance. This gives you time to see slowing or stopped vehicles and brake smoothly instead of stopping abruptly.

question: On a roadway divided by double solid yellow lines, when are you allowed to cross them?
options: a:Only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:To pass slower vehicles if no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Never under any circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean you must not use the opposing lane to pass. However, you may carefully cross them to make a left turn into or from an alley, side street, private road, or driveway when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: You may cross double solid yellow lines to:
options: a:Pass a slow-moving vehicle.,b:Change lanes at any time.,c:Use the shoulder to pass.,d:Turn into a driveway or make a left turn where it is permitted.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing or lane changes across the lines because they separate opposing traffic. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or to make another permitted left turn when it is safe.

question: Which statement about littering from a vehicle is true?
options: a:Littering is illegal and can lead to fines or jail time.,b:Littering is not regulated.,c:Littering rarely causes accidents.
note: Throwing trash or objects from a vehicle is illegal in every state. Litter can create road hazards, distract drivers, or cause them to swerve, leading to crashes. Convictions can bring fines, community service, and in some cases even jail time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes from the right lane into the left on a multilane highway, what should you check?
options: a:Only your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.,b:Over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Turn on your directional signal and immediately swerve left.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and then look over your shoulder in the direction you’re moving to check your blind spot. A quick glance over your left shoulder confirms there is no vehicle hidden beside you before you move into the left lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn on a multilane one-way street?
options: a:The left lane.,b:The right lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: On a one-way street with multiple lanes, you must start a left turn from the leftmost lane that is lawfully available. This keeps you out of the path of traffic going straight and lines you up correctly with the proper lane on the street you are turning onto.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Stop completely, then proceed when the way is clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Wait until the light turns green before moving.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians in all directions, and then proceed only when it is safe and the way is clear.

question: What does a red arrow signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow is displayed.,b:Slow and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and then proceed when clear even if the arrow remains red.
note: A red arrow means you may not enter the intersection to move in the direction of that arrow. You must stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears that allows movement in that direction.

question: What actions should you take when approaching a railroad crossing?
options: a:Slow down, look, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to clear the tracks quickly.,c:Assume the crossing is clear unless gates are down.
note: When approaching a railroad crossing, reduce speed, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be prepared to stop. If warning lights, gates, or a flagger indicate a train is coming, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail and remain stopped until it is safe to cross.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of you, what is the correct action?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,b:Flash your lights.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Drivers must always be prepared to yield to pedestrians. When someone begins crossing in front of you, slow down, be ready to stop, and give them the right-of-way, especially when they are in a crosswalk or at an intersection.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the left side mirror.,b:Look into the rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; areas not visible in your mirrors are blind spots. Before changing lanes, quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop even if no traffic is present.,b:Slow down and yield to traffic in or approaching the roadway you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic on the right.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let any traffic, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in the intersection or close enough to be a hazard go first. If the way is clear, you do not have to stop, but you must still approach at a safe, reduced speed.

question: Which conditions can impair a person's ability to drive safely?
options: a:A lack of sleep.,b:Alcohol.,c:Both sleep deprivation and alcohol can impair driving.
note: Both alcohol and lack of sleep reduce your ability to drive safely. They slow your reaction time, harm your judgment, and make it harder to stay alert and in your lane. Any time you are drowsy or have been drinking, you are not fit to drive.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,b:When exiting an expressway only.,c:Only when following a motorcycle.
note: You should leave more space in front of you whenever conditions make it harder to see or stop in time. This includes following large vehicles that block your view, driving in bad weather, heavy traffic, when exiting a freeway, and when following motorcycles or bicycles, which can stop or fall more quickly.

question: What do two solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed.,c:Passing is allowed when going over a hill.
note: Two solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean vehicles in both directions may not cross the lines to pass. You must stay in your lane and only cross when making a permitted left turn into or from a driveway or side road, if allowed by local law.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The combination may multiply the impairing effects of either the alcohol or the medicine.,b:The medicine negates the alcohol's effects.,c:Alcohol helps the medicine work better.
note: Alcohol combined with prescription or over‑the‑counter medicine can greatly increase drowsiness, dizziness, and slowed reactions. The effects can be stronger and more unpredictable than either substance alone, making it very dangerous to drive.

question: Which of the following is a restriction for an intermediate driver's license?
options: a:No passengers at any time.,b:Driving curfew between 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. except for school/activity/job or emergency.,c:No seat belt required for the driver.
note: An intermediate (provisional) license typically includes a late-night driving restriction, often between about 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m., unless the driver is going to or from work, school activities, or in an emergency. Seat belts are required for all occupants, and there is no rule that bans all passengers at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection that is blocked with traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.,c:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it. If traffic ahead is stopped and you would be left blocking the intersection, you must wait behind the stop line until there is enough space to drive all the way through.

question: What do highway pavement markings and other roadway markings provide for drivers?
options: a:Are usually not important.,b:Are only found in construction zones.,c:Provide information for drivers.
note: Pavement and roadway markings give important information such as lane use, passing zones, turn lanes, crosswalks, and warnings about changes in the road. Drivers must pay attention to these markings to stay in the correct lane and drive safely.

question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving at excessive speeds on wet roads causing tires to ride on a film of water.,b:Excessive stops.,c:Sudden turns at low speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when you drive fast on wet roads and your tires cannot push the water away. The tires then ride on a thin film of water instead of gripping the pavement, which can cause loss of steering and braking control.

question: Which device increases crash risk when used while driving:
options: a:A CD player.,b:A cell phone.,c:A radio.
note: Using a cell phone while driving, even hands‑free, takes your attention away from the road and greatly increases crash risk. Visual, manual, and mental distraction from calls, texts, or apps makes it harder to react quickly to traffic conditions.

question: Which driving practice helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Get off the highway immediately.,b:Add extra weight to the vehicle to improve traction.,c:Reduce speed and increase following distance.
note: On snow or ice, tires have much less grip, so you need more time and space to react. Reducing speed lowers the force of any potential impact and makes it easier to steer and stop. Increasing your following distance gives you extra room to brake gently and avoid skids. Adding weight is not a reliable or recommended way to improve traction for normal passenger vehicles.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:Work zones or construction ahead.,b:School zones.,c:Regulatory requirements like stop or speed limits.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in work zones. They warn of construction, maintenance, or utility work and may indicate lane shifts, reduced speeds, or workers and equipment on or near the roadway. School zones use yellow or fluorescent yellow‑green signs, and regulatory signs like STOP or speed limits are typically white with black or red lettering.

question: When you are approached by an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren, you must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right and turn on your vehicle's four-way flashers.,b:Pull to the right and slow down.,c:Pull to the right and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and/or siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right as safely possible and stopping until it has passed. Stopping makes your actions predictable and gives the emergency vehicle a clear path. You should not just slow down or keep moving unless directed otherwise by a police officer or it is physically impossible to pull over.

question: A solid white edge line on the right that slants left indicates what ahead?
options: a:The road is narrowing ahead.,b:An intersection is ahead.,c:A left turn is required ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the outer edge of the roadway. When this line slants or angles toward the center of the road, it is warning you that the usable roadway is about to become narrower. This may happen on bridges, in construction areas, or where shoulders disappear, so you should be prepared to adjust your position and speed.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what should you first do?
options: a:Stop at or near the scene.,b:Call the police immediately without stopping.,c:Drive home and report it later.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at or as close to the scene as safely possible. Once stopped, check for injuries and, if you can, move vehicles out of traffic to prevent another collision. Call 911 if anyone is hurt or if there is major damage. Leaving the scene without stopping is illegal and can result in serious penalties.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:Begin to cross immediately since one train has passed.,b:Always stop before crossing even if no train is visible.,c:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.,d:Speed up to clear the tracks quickly.
note: When there are multiple tracks, one train passing can hide another coming from the opposite direction or on the other track. After the first train clears, you must look carefully and listen for a second train on any track and only proceed when you are sure all tracks are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Early enough for others to know your intention before you change lanes.,b:Only after you begin the lane change.,c:Only if other traffic is present.
note: You must signal before you change lanes or begin passing so other drivers have time to see your signal and react. Signaling only as you move, or only when you see other traffic, does not give enough warning and can lead to collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is never dangerous if you are a skilled driver.,c:Speed does not affect crash severity.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic on certain roads can cause sudden braking, lane changes, and rear‑end crashes. Both speeding and driving too slowly for conditions are dangerous, and higher speeds greatly increase crash severity because impact forces rise with speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is correct when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and ensure no oncoming traffic.,b:Use mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,c:Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.,d:All of the above
note: Safe passing requires several steps: signal in advance (typically at least 100 feet before changing lanes), check mirrors and look over your shoulder to clear your blind spot, and only return to your lane when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle—usually both headlights—in your rearview mirror.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal signify?
options: a:Proceed with caution and slow down.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to cross quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed carefully. Be prepared to yield to pedestrians and cross traffic that may be entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns green, what is required before you proceed?
options: a:Accelerate as fast as possible to clear the intersection.,b:Back up slowly if needed.,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.
note: A green light means you may go only after you first check the intersection and yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles still in the intersection. You must not move until it is safe and clear, even if the light is green.

question: Where is it legal to consume alcoholic beverages inside a vehicle on a public road?
options: a:It may be illegal for the driver and, in many states, for passengers to consume or possess open alcoholic beverages; laws vary by state.,b:It is always legal for passengers in the back seat to drink alcohol.,c:It is always legal to drink alcohol in the bed of a pickup truck.
note: Open‑container and in‑vehicle drinking rules vary by state. In many states, passengers are allowed to possess or sometimes consume alcohol in certain seating positions, while the driver may not. Because the legality depends on state law, there is no single rule that says it is never legal anywhere in the U.S. to consume or possess alcohol in a vehicle on a public road. Always check your specific state’s open‑container and passenger‑consumption laws.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist going in the same direction?
options: a:Slow down and wait until no oncoming traffic is present, then pass with sufficient space.,b:Blow your horn and pass closely but quickly.,c:Never pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: On a two‑lane road without a bike lane, treat a bicycle like a slow‑moving vehicle. Slow down, wait for a safe gap in oncoming traffic, then move over and pass with plenty of space—at least 3 feet, and more at higher speeds. Never squeeze past a bicyclist in the same lane when oncoming traffic is close.

question: Is it permissible to drive around or under a crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,b:If an approaching train is not too close.,c:No — do not drive around or under a moving gate.
note: When railroad crossing lights are flashing or the gate is moving or down, you must stop and stay behind the gate. Never drive around, under, or through a moving or lowered gate, even if you do not see a train. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the gate is fully raised before proceeding.

question: If you drive while intoxicated and cause injury or death to another person, what are possible consequences?
options: a:You will only have to pay a fine.,b:You will only lose your license.,c:You may face jail time, fines, and license loss.
note: Driving while intoxicated and causing injury or death is a very serious crime. You can be sentenced to jail or prison, fined heavily, and lose your driving privileges for a long period. Civil lawsuits from victims or their families are also possible, in addition to criminal penalties.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Keep a steady pace.,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,c:Stay in the driver's blind spot.
note: Blind spots are areas alongside and slightly behind a vehicle that the driver cannot see in their mirrors. If you are riding in another driver’s blind spot, they may change lanes or turn into you without realizing you are there. You should either move ahead so you are clearly visible in their mirrors or drop back so they can see you, and avoid lingering in that hidden area.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:The traffic signal is changing from green to red.,b:You should slam on your brakes immediately.,c:You should increase your speed to clear the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should prepare to stop and do so if you can safely stop before entering the intersection. Do not slam on the brakes if it would cause a rear-end collision, and do not speed up to “beat” the red light, which is unsafe and often illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left and opposing traffic blocks your view, what is the correct action?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane is clear.,b:Wait until you can see all the lanes you must cross before making the turn.,c:Rely on an oncoming driver to wave you through.
note: When turning left across oncoming traffic, you must not start your turn until you can clearly see all lanes you must cross and are sure you can complete the turn safely. Never rely on another driver waving you through, and do not accelerate blindly when only one lane appears clear; hidden vehicles or changing traffic can create a serious collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you allow the other vehicle?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.
note: On narrow two-way roads, each driver must allow the other at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the roadway so both vehicles can pass safely. You should slow down, keep as far to the right as is safe, and share the available space rather than forcing the other driver off the road or demanding they yield all the room.

question: What is the only effective way to reduce your BAC?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) goes down only as your body processes the alcohol over time. Coffee, exercise, cold showers, or other tricks may make you feel more awake but do not speed up how quickly your liver removes alcohol from your bloodstream. The only safe way to lower BAC is to wait long enough before driving.

question: Which actions help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires with good tread and proper inflation and reduce speed in rain.,b:Increase speed to cut through the water.,c:Ignore tire condition if roads look clear.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. Good tread and proper tire pressure help channel water away, and slowing down in rain reduces the chance your tires will lose grip.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Try to drive around a lowered gate.,b:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,c:Speed up to cross before the gate is lowered.
note: At railroad crossings you must approach carefully: slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be ready to stop. Never go around lowered gates or try to beat a train; trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right of way.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what should you allow the rider to use?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,c:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane just like any other vehicle. Giving them the entire lane provides space to maneuver, avoid hazards, and maintain a safe following distance from other traffic.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted on the roadway?
options: a:In curves and on hills.,b:Next to churches and schools.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes at intersections and crosswalks to show exactly where you must stop for a stop sign or red light, before entering the crosswalk or intersection.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:When pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:When turning left or right.,c:When changing lanes or otherwise moving sideways in traffic (such as merging or pulling toward or away from a curb).
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You should quickly glance over your shoulder to check these areas whenever you change lanes or move sideways in traffic, such as when merging or pulling toward or away from a curb, to be sure the space is clear.

question: Must traffic signs and pavement markings be obeyed?
options: a:Yes, they must always be obeyed.,b:No, they are only suggestions.,c:Only when other traffic is present.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls, not suggestions. You must always obey them because they tell you when to stop, go, yield, change lanes, or adjust speed, which keeps traffic orderly and prevents crashes.

question: How does driving faster affect tire performance on a wet roadway?
options: a:The faster you drive, the less effective your tires become at clearing water.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: On wet roads, higher speeds make it harder for tires to push water out of the way. As speed increases, a thin layer of water can build between the tire and the road, reducing traction and increasing the risk of hydroplaning.

question: When is horn use appropriate in emergency situations?
options: a:To warn others if you have lost control of your vehicle.,b:To express anger at another driver.,c:To greet pedestrians.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger, such as when you are losing control or another driver is about to hit you. Do not use the horn to show anger or to greet people, because unnecessary honking can startle others and create unsafe situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,c:Either driver may proceed without yielding.
note: At an uncontrolled or open intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the right may proceed first, but both drivers should move only when it is clearly safe.

question: If a driver is aggressive behind you, what is the best action?
options: a:Stare at the driver as he or she passes you.,b:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.,c:Speed up as he or she is passing you.
note: When another driver is aggressive or tailgating, do not engage with them. Safely move to another lane or otherwise allow them to pass, and avoid eye contact or gestures. Creating space between you and the aggressive driver reduces the chance of a collision.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When the lights stop flashing.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the train has passed and gates lift.
note: You must never drive around lowered railroad crossing gates. Lowered gates and flashing lights mean a train is approaching or is nearby, and it is both illegal and extremely dangerous to go around them, even if you do not immediately see a train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean for turning drivers?
options: a:It means drivers may turn in the indicated direction without restriction.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light—prepare to stop.,c:It is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light: the signal is about to turn red, so you should prepare to stop if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, complete your turn with caution before the light changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:Yes.,b:No.,c:Only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, not to pass.
note: You may not cross double solid yellow lines to pass another vehicle. Double solid yellow lines mark areas where passing is prohibited in both directions because of limited visibility or other safety concerns. You may, however, cross them carefully to turn left into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley when it is safe.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what must you be prepared to do?
options: a:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,b:Speed across the crossing before the train arrives.,c:Look for a way around lowered gates.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching tracks and must slow down, look, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby or signals are activated, and never try to beat a train or go around lowered gates.

question: What is a likely consequence of a second DWI conviction within five years in Missouri?
options: a:Have your driving privilege denied for a lengthy period, not just 90 days.,b:Face serious sanctions that affect all driving, not just residential roads.,c:Be required to install an Ignition Interlock Device (IID) before reinstatement.
note: In Missouri, a second DWI within five years is treated very seriously. It can result in a long license denial period, substantial fines, possible jail time, and a requirement to install an Ignition Interlock Device (IID) before your driving privilege can be reinstated. The IID helps prevent further impaired driving by requiring a breath test before the vehicle will start.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the skid.,c:Keep the front wheels straight.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This helps you regain control. As the vehicle starts to straighten out, you may need to steer gently in the other direction to avoid overcorrecting. Avoid jerking the wheel or braking hard, as that can make the skid worse.

question: After purchasing a vehicle, within what time must you apply for the title?
options: a:Within 30 days.,b:Within six months.,c:Within one week.
note: Many states require you to apply for a vehicle title within 30 days of purchase, but this time limit is set by each state and is not the same nationwide. Some states allow less time and others more. Always check your own state’s DMV rules for the exact deadline to avoid penalties.

question: Which recommendation would generally not improve nighttime driving safety?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Be aware tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.,c:Drive with your interior dome light on to read maps.
note: For safer night driving, keep your windshield and windows clean and be aware that dark window tint can make it harder to see at night. Do not drive with the interior dome light on to read; the light causes glare on the glass and reduces your ability to see outside, especially in low‑light conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your vehicle be positioned when making a right turn?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:As close to the right side of the road as possible.
note: When making a right turn, you should be in the rightmost lane or as close to the right edge of the roadway as is safe and legal. This position makes your intentions clear to other drivers, shortens the turn, and reduces the chance of a collision with vehicles going straight or turning from other lanes.

question: In traffic, what is the safest way to drive relative to the flow of traffic?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.,b:Fluctuate your speed to keep alert.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic within posted limits.
note: The safest practice is to drive at a speed that matches the flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit and adjusting for conditions. Driving much faster or slower than surrounding traffic increases the risk of conflicts and crashes because other drivers must brake, change lanes, or pass unexpectedly.

question: After a minor collision that leaves your vehicle blocking traffic, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Not move your vehicle under any circumstances.,b:Wait until the police arrive before moving your vehicle.,c:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.
note: After a minor collision, if no one is seriously injured and the vehicles are drivable, you should move your vehicle out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or another safe location. This helps prevent additional crashes and keeps traffic flowing. Once safely out of the way, exchange information and identify yourself to the other driver.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:They are limited to the bicycle lane.,b:They are entitled to the same full lane width as other vehicles.,c:They get half the lane width.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full traffic lane just like cars and trucks. Other drivers should not crowd a motorcycle in its lane or try to share the lane side‑by‑side with it. Giving motorcycles the full lane helps them maintain balance, avoid hazards, and stop safely.

question: What is the safest way to handle a driver tailgating you?
options: a:Gradually slow down or change lanes to encourage them to pass.,b:Slam on your brakes to signal them to back off.,c:Speed up to increase the gap ahead of you.
note: When another driver is following too closely, the safest response is to stay calm, gradually reduce your speed, and, when safe, change lanes or otherwise allow them to pass. Do not slam on your brakes or speed up, as both can increase the risk of a collision and escalate the situation.

question: Which of these is a common cause of distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,b:Changing a radio station or CD.,c:Talking or texting on a cell phone.,d:All of the above.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. Eating, drinking, smoking, changing the radio, and especially talking or texting on a cell phone are all common distractions that increase crash risk. Texting is particularly dangerous because it combines visual, manual, and cognitive distraction.

question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A solid green light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A green arrow pointing left
note: A steady green left arrow means you have a protected left turn: oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing you are stopped by a red light, so you have the right‑of‑way to turn left. A solid green light or flashing yellow arrow usually requires you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green turn arrow changes to a steady green light, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.,b:You can no longer turn and must go straight.,c:You keep the right-of-way to turn without yielding.
note: When a green turn arrow changes to a steady green light, the protected turn ends. You may still turn, but now oncoming traffic has a green light too. You must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk, and only turn when it is safe.

question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Obey all traffic signals and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Drive around lowered crossing gates.,c:Assume trains will yield to cars.
note: At light rail or train crossings, you must always obey all traffic signals and warning devices and never drive around lowered gates. Trains cannot stop quickly, so you must look both ways and be sure the tracks are clear before crossing.

question: How can you reduce your chance of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Drive through shallow water quickly.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Reduce your speed.
