note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds. The best way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning is to slow down on wet roads and drive smoothly, especially in heavy rain or standing water.

question: What is the fee for an instruction permit in Missouri?
note: Missouri’s instruction permit fee is $2.00. An instruction permit allows a new driver to practice driving while supervised by a properly licensed adult, helping them gain experience before driving alone.

question: Which of the following is not an effect of alcohol on driving?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You are less alert.
note: Alcohol negatively affects many parts of driving ability: it slows reflexes and reaction time, distorts judgment of speed and distance, and makes you less alert. Because all of the listed choices are true effects of alcohol, none of them is correct as an answer to “Which is NOT an effect?” A better question would ask which IS an effect of alcohol, with all three as correct examples.

question: How can you help avoid rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops and allow your vehicle to slow before applying brakes.,b:Ignore mirrors and focus on the vehicle ahead.,c:Brake sharply without warning to alert those behind you.
note: To reduce the risk of being hit from behind, start slowing by easing off the accelerator early and then braking smoothly and gradually. Avoid sudden, hard stops whenever possible so drivers behind you have enough time and distance to react.

question: Which actions improve safety when driving at night?
options: a:Increase following distance and ensure headlights are working.,b:Drive only if you are tired.,c:Use high beams at all times.
note: At night, visibility is reduced, so you should increase your following distance and make sure your headlights and taillights are clean and working properly. Avoid driving when you are tired, and use high beams only when appropriate—never when following another vehicle closely or when there is oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to the driving lane?
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.,c:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.
note: After passing, do not move back into the lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and there is a safe gap. This ensures you are not cutting too closely in front of the other driver and reduces the chance of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing for a left turn, what checks should you make?
options: a:Signal early, check mirrors and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Only check your rearview mirror.,c:Speed up and cut across traffic.
note: Before a left turn, signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and watch for oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and cyclists. You must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk before turning, making the turn only when it is safe and clear.

question: Where should you maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in front of your vehicle.,b:On all sides of your vehicle.,c:Only behind your vehicle.
note: A space cushion on all sides of your vehicle gives you room to maneuver and time to react if another driver makes a mistake or a hazard appears. Maintain safe following distance in front, avoid tailgaters behind when possible, and keep side space by not driving directly next to other vehicles for long periods.

question: If a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws, what can happen?
options: a:They can be ticketed like motor vehicle drivers.,b:They are always given only a warning.,c:They are exempt from traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists are generally required to follow the same traffic laws as motor vehicle drivers. When they disobey traffic laws—such as running stop signs or ignoring traffic signals—they can be stopped and ticketed just like drivers of cars.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing another vehicle is prohibited in which situation?
options: a:When the road is wet.,b:Only when there are no lane markings.,c:Whenever the vehicle ahead is signaling a turn.,d:On hills and curves.
note: Passing is prohibited where your view of oncoming traffic is limited, such as on hills and curves, because you cannot be sure the opposing lane is clear for the entire passing maneuver. It is also typically illegal at intersections and railroad crossings for the same visibility and safety reasons.

question: At a stop sign, which sequence of observations is recommended before proceeding?
options: a:Look left first, then right, then left again.,b:Check your rearview mirror first, then go.,c:Move as soon as the vehicle ahead moves.
note: At a stop sign, you should first look left, where traffic is closer to you in the lane you will enter, then look right, and then look left again before proceeding. This left–right–left pattern helps you detect vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists that may be approaching from either direction.

question: What does SATOP stand for?
options: a:Salt And Tar On Pavement.,b:Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program.,c:Steer At The Other Point.
note: SATOP stands for Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program. Many states require drivers convicted of certain alcohol- or drug-related driving offenses to complete this program as part of license reinstatement or sentencing.

question: What should you do to be ready for anything ahead on the road?
options: a:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Continuously scan the entire road and roadsides.
note: To be prepared for hazards, you should constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and check mirrors regularly. This wide scanning helps you spot problems early—such as slowing traffic, pedestrians, or debris—so you have time to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At stop signs, red lights, or when ordered by a traffic officer.,b:Only when other vehicles are present.,c:Only at intersections with no visible cross traffic.
note: You must come to a complete stop at stop signs, red traffic lights, and any time a police officer or authorized traffic officer directs you to stop. You may also need to stop for pedestrians in crosswalks, school buses with flashing red lights, and emergency vehicles, but answer A correctly covers the basic legal requirements listed.

question: Pentagon-shaped traffic signs are used to indicate:
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones and school crossings.,c:Speed limits.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: Pentagon-shaped (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane or on a multilane road going in your direction.,b:If it requires driving off the paved surface.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right only when it can be done safely and without leaving the paved roadway. This is typically allowed when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a clearly marked lane to the right, or on multilane roads where traffic moves in the same direction. You must never drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass.

question: When changing lanes, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to verify your blind spot is clear before moving.,b:Rely solely on your mirrors.,c:Signal at least 100–200 feet in advance, then change lanes without checking your blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal to let others know your intention, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, and then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on mirrors, because vehicles can be hidden in areas your mirrors do not show.

question: What is the most common color for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Most general warning signs are yellow with black symbols or lettering and are often diamond-shaped. They alert you to conditions such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or other potential hazards ahead so you can slow down and proceed with caution.

question: What does a black symbol on a yellow diamond-shaped sign generally tell you?
options: a:Warning about conditions on or near the road.,b:Directions to cities and towns.,c:Traffic laws and regulations.
note: Yellow diamond-shaped signs with black symbols are warning signs. They alert you to conditions or hazards on or near the road ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or animal crossings, so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you begin to lose traction, what should you do with the brake pedal?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Release the brake pedal and coast.
note: With ABS (antilock braking system), you should press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup so you can maintain steering control while braking hard.

question: What do downward-pointing triangular traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:A school zone.,b:Yield to other traffic.,c:A construction area.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the shape used for yield signs. When you see this sign, slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in a line at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after the vehicles ahead have gone through, what must you do?
options: a:You may proceed without stopping again.,b:You must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before going.,c:You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
note: At a stop sign, each vehicle must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, even if cars ahead of you have already stopped and gone. After stopping, yield as needed, then proceed when it is safe.

question: When there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Pass the bicyclist immediately and squeeze by the car.,b:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist so you handle only one hazard at a time.,c:Split the difference and squeeze between both.
note: When facing an oncoming car and a bicyclist at the same time, do not try to squeeze between them. Let the oncoming car pass first, then move over and pass the bicyclist with plenty of space so you only handle one hazard at a time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best approach?
options: a:Use the ramp to accelerate to freeway speed and blend into traffic.,b:Proceed slowly and wait for a large gap.,c:Turn on hazard lights while merging.
note: When entering a freeway, use the on‑ramp to accelerate to the speed of traffic so you can merge smoothly. Always yield to vehicles already on the freeway and adjust your speed and gap so you blend safely into the flow.

question: If involved in an accident, which actions should a driver take?
options: a:Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.,c:Turn off the ignition(s) of wrecked vehicles.,d:All of the above
note: After a collision, you must stop at or near the scene, avoid standing or walking in traffic lanes, and, if it is safe, turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles to reduce fire risk. Move vehicles out of traffic if possible and call for emergency help when needed.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, liquor) change how it affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Beer impairs you less than wine.,b:Hard ciders and mixed drinks impair you most.,c:No — impairment depends on the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream, not the beverage type.
note: Beer, wine, and liquor all affect you the same way if they contain the same amount of alcohol. Impairment depends on your blood alcohol concentration, which is determined by how much alcohol you consume, not the type of drink.

question: How should you respond to an approaching emergency vehicle using lights and siren?
options: a:Continue driving but attempt to remain out of its path.,b:Try to reach your destination before it gets to you.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop until it has passed.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as you safely can and stopping until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, how should you proceed?
options: a:Always stop before crossing.,b:Cross quickly without looking.,c:Be prepared to yield to any approaching train and make sure you have room to clear the tracks.
note: At a railroad crossing without flashing lights or gates, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop. Never start across unless you are sure no train is coming and there is enough room for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks on the far side.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Have done as much as you can.,b:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and circumstances of the accident.,c:Must stay until the police arrive.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must stop and leave a written note in a secure, visible place on the vehicle. The note must include your name, address, and a brief description of what happened so the owner can contact you and make an insurance claim.

question: What do orange-colored signs generally indicate?
options: a:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:A railroad crossing is ahead.
note: Orange signs are used for temporary traffic control in work or incident areas. They warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations and alert you to slow down, be prepared for workers and equipment, and expect lane shifts or other changes in normal traffic patterns.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may pass or change lanes if it is safe.,b:Drivers may not pass.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle is using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:You must yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right and stopping until the emergency vehicle has passed.,b:You may follow closely behind the emergency vehicle to move through traffic faster.,c:You may ignore it and continue in your lane if you have a green light.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and flashing lights, you must immediately yield the right‑of‑way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed, unless otherwise directed by a police officer or the emergency vehicle’s loudspeaker. Stay alert for additional emergency vehicles that may be following.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull next to the driver and yell at them.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Flash your high beams at them to show your displeasure.
note: If another driver cuts you off, stay calm and do not retaliate. Slow slightly if needed to re‑establish a safe following distance and continue driving defensively. Aggressive responses like yelling, honking excessively, or flashing high beams can escalate the situation into road rage and increase the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:Either one,b:The vehicle on the left,c:The vehicle on the right
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions by clearly assigning right‑of‑way.

question: What is the effect of combining drugs with alcohol on crash risk?
options: a:It decreases the risk of causing a crash.,b:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,c:It has no effect on your ability to drive.
note: Alcohol and many drugs both affect judgment, coordination, and reaction time. When they are combined, their effects are often multiplied, not just added, which greatly increases your chances of causing a crash.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.,b:All railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.,c:You never have to stop when directed by a flagger.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad gates; it is illegal and extremely dangerous. Not all crossings have lights or gates, so you must always look and listen for trains and obey any flagger or signal present.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what is the proper response?
options: a:Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass anywhere.,b:Proceed slowly and permit the vehicle to pass without pulling over.,c:Drive as far toward the right side of the road as is safe and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must move as far to the right side of the road as is safe and stop until it has passed. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: What is the minimum age to obtain a motorcycle instruction permit in Missouri?
options: a:14 years old.,b:15 years old.,c:15 and one-half years old.
note: In Missouri, you must be at least 15½ years old to obtain a motorcycle instruction permit. This permit allows you to practice riding under specific restrictions before getting a full motorcycle license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.,b:Continue through if no other vehicles are present.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Come to a complete stop; you may turn right on red unless a sign prohibits it.
note: A steady red light requires a complete stop. After stopping, you may turn right on red unless a sign forbids it; running red lights is illegal and dangerous.

question: Where will the Driver License Bureau mail your renewal reminder postcard shortly before expiry?
options: a:To the address on your last application.,b:To the address listed in the phone book.,c:To the mailing address on your driver record.
note: Renewal notices are mailed to the mailing address shown on your driver record. It is your responsibility to keep your address current with the licensing agency so that important notices, including renewal reminders, can reach you.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a vehicle?
options: a:Your seat position.,b:Your mirrors only.,c:Your safety belt only.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can comfortably reach the pedals, steering wheel, and controls and have a clear view of the road. Once your seating position is correct, adjust your mirrors and steering wheel, then fasten your safety belt before driving.

question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is on your side, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:Only if you are on an expressway.,c:You may pass if traffic is clear and it is safe to do so.
note: A solid yellow line means no passing from that side, while a broken yellow line means passing is allowed when safe. If the broken yellow line is on your side of the center, you may cross it to pass another vehicle, but only when there is enough clear distance ahead and no oncoming traffic or other hazards.

question: If you fail the driving test three times, what will the examiner do?
options: a:You must reapply for a learner's permit.,b:The Department will require additional behind-the-wheel training before retesting.,c:You may retake the test the next day without restriction.,d:The examiner will give you a Driving Skills Examination Report to send to the Department of Revenue.
note: If you fail the driving test three times, the examiner will issue a Driving Skills Examination Report. You must send this report to the Department of Revenue, which will review your record and let you know if you must complete additional behind‑the‑wheel training or meet other requirements before testing again.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see and may be hidden in blind spots.,b:Motorcyclists rarely follow traffic laws.,c:Motorcyclists always travel at high speeds.
note: Motorcycles are smaller than most vehicles and can be easily hidden in blind spots or masked by other traffic, roadside objects, or weather conditions. Because they are narrower, it can also be harder to judge their speed and distance. Always check mirrors and blind spots carefully and allow extra following and passing space around motorcycles.

question: How does increasing your vehicle’s speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision narrows and you see less to the sides (reduced peripheral vision). This makes it easier to miss pedestrians, cyclists, and cross traffic. Slowing down gives you a wider view of the road and more time to react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes or passing on an interstate?
options: a:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.,b:Always use cruise control.,c:Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spots.
note: Before changing lanes or passing on an interstate, always signal to communicate your intentions, check your mirrors, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This ensures there is enough space and that no vehicle is hidden beside you. Only stop on the shoulder for emergencies, and use cruise control only when conditions are safe.

question: What must you do when a flagger is controlling traffic in a construction zone?
options: a:Follow the flagger's directions.,b:Ignore the flagger and follow surrounding traffic.,c:Assume the flagger's directions are optional.
note: Flaggers in construction zones have the same authority as traffic signals or signs. You must obey their directions, even if they differ from normal traffic patterns. Following their instructions protects road workers and drivers and helps traffic move safely through the work area.

question: If you are at fault in a crash and fail to pay for damages, what can happen to your driving privileges?
options: a:Your driver license and/or plates will be suspended for one year.,b:You will save money.,c:Your car will be repossessed automatically.
note: If you are at fault in a crash and do not pay for the damages or make acceptable arrangements, your driver license and/or vehicle registration can be suspended, often for up to a year or until you show proof of payment or settlement. Financial responsibility laws are designed to ensure that drivers can cover the costs of injuries or property damage they cause.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, when should you allow a larger space cushion in front of your vehicle?
options: a:When stopped at a stop sign on level ground.,b:Whenever you are stopped on an uphill incline.,c:When stopped at an intersection on level ground.
note: When you are stopped on an uphill slope, you should leave extra space in front of your vehicle at all times. If the vehicle ahead rolls backward when starting, the larger space cushion gives you time and room to react and avoid a rear‑end collision.

question: What important attribute do large trucks have that car drivers should remember?
options: a:They have large blind spots.,b:They can stop more quickly than cars.,c:They do not need extra maneuvering room.
note: Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than passenger cars, especially directly behind, along both sides, and sometimes in front of the cab. If you drive in these areas, the truck driver may not see you. Stay out of these blind spots when possible and give trucks extra space for stopping and turning.

question: What does a green traffic arrow mean for the lane it controls?
options: a:You may proceed only if a circular green is also lit.,b:It is used only on one-way streets.,c:Traffic in that lane may proceed in the direction of the arrow when it is green, after yielding to traffic and pedestrians still in the intersection.
note: A green arrow means traffic in that specific lane is allowed to move only in the direction of the arrow, and oncoming traffic, bicycles, and pedestrians are usually stopped by a red light. You may proceed in the direction of the arrow after yielding to any traffic or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: Regarding pedestrians, what responsibility does a driver have?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian is always aware of their vehicle.,b:Always use every reasonable precaution to avoid hitting pedestrians and be prepared to yield to them to prevent a collision.,c:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.
note: Drivers must use every reasonable precaution to avoid hitting pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly. You are required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections, and you should slow down or stop if necessary to prevent a collision, regardless of who technically has the right‑of‑way.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should a driver of a small vehicle be prepared for?
options: a:Loud noises.,b:Excess air pollution.,c:Wind gusts caused by the large vehicle.
note: When you pass or are passed by a large truck or bus, the air it pushes aside can create strong wind gusts. These gusts can cause your smaller vehicle to sway or drift in your lane. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be prepared to make small steering corrections to stay in control.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your driving?
options: a:It does not affect driving abilities.,b:It helps maintain alertness.,c:It is a distracting activity.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is distracting because it takes at least one hand off the wheel and often your eyes off the road to handle the cigarette, lighter, or ashes. Any activity that diverts your attention, hands, or eyes from driving increases the risk of a crash.

question: What effect does alcohol have on reflexes and reaction time?
options: a:It speeds them up.,b:It slows them down.,c:It has no effect.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain processing, which delays your reflexes and reaction time. This means you take longer to notice hazards and longer to move your foot from the gas to the brake, making it much harder to avoid collisions.

question: If you are being tailgated, what is the safest action?
options: a:Brake abruptly to warn the tailgater.,b:Move to the right if an open lane exists; if not, slow gradually to encourage them to pass.,c:Increase your speed so the tailgater must back off.
note: When someone is following too closely, your goal is to reduce risk, not “teach them a lesson.” If there is a clear lane to your right, safely move over and let them pass. If you cannot change lanes, gradually slow down to increase the following distance and encourage them to go around you. Never brake abruptly, because that can cause a rear-end collision.

question: Regulatory signs are intended to:
options: a:Tell drivers what actions are required or prohibited.,b:Warn about upcoming hazards only.,c:Provide mileage information.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do under the law, such as speed limits, stop signs, yield signs, and turn restrictions. Drivers are legally required to obey these signs because they set the rules for safe and orderly traffic flow.

question: What is the correct initial positioning when preparing to parallel park between two vehicles?
options: a:Stop even with the car in front of the space.,b:Turn wheels immediately to the left.,c:Back up directly into the space without aligning.
note: For parallel parking, you first pull up alongside and stop even with the vehicle in front of the space, leaving a safe side gap. From this position, you can then back slowly while turning the wheel to angle your car into the space under control. Turning the wheels too early or backing in without aligning makes it difficult to enter the space safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection, stop line, or crosswalk.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the stop line, crosswalk, or entering the intersection, and remain stopped until the light turns green or you are allowed to turn on red where permitted by law.

question: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct way to return to the road?
options: a:Stop quickly and then turn sharply onto the pavement.,b:Take your foot off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow, and ease back onto the pavement.,c:Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, keep the vehicle steering straight and parallel to the road, slow down gradually, and then gently steer back onto the pavement when traffic and road conditions make it safe.

question: What is the safest practice before backing a vehicle?
options: a:Walk to the rear of the vehicle to check for children or objects.,b:Honk the horn before shifting into reverse.,c:Rely solely on rearview mirrors.
note: Before backing, walk behind your vehicle to check for children, pedestrians, and objects you cannot see from the driver’s seat. Then back up slowly while checking mirrors and looking over your shoulder, because visibility is limited when reversing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is that hand signal indicating?
options: a:Come to a stop.,b:Turn left.,c:Turn right.
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm straight out indicates a left turn, a left arm bent upward at the elbow indicates a right turn, and a left arm bent downward indicates slowing or stopping.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means vehicles traveling in either direction are not allowed to pass. You may cross the lines only to make a left turn or to enter or leave a driveway or side road when it is safe.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both will always be reduced.,d:Only alcohol effects increase.
note: Alcohol can interact with many drugs, including prescription, over‑the‑counter, and illegal drugs, in a way that increases drowsiness, slows reaction time, and impairs judgment more than either substance alone. Because of this additive or even multiplying effect, you can become dangerously impaired with smaller amounts than you might expect.

question: What color lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: White lane lines are used to separate traffic moving in the same direction, such as on multi‑lane roads and freeways. A broken white line means you may change lanes when it is safe, while a solid white line discourages or prohibits lane changes in that area.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes.,b:Pull to the right side of the road and stop.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass ahead of you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and/or flashing lights, you must yield the right‑of‑way by moving as far to the right side of the road as possible and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs you otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right.,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
note: When parking facing downhill on a two‑way street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will touch the curb and help stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: What do functioning brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:That you are slowing down or stopping.,b:That you are changing lanes.,c:That your emergency brake is engaged.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. This gives them time to reduce speed or change lanes safely, helping to prevent rear‑end collisions. You should check regularly to make sure your brake lights work properly.

question: What defines a driver's blind spot?
options: a:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,b:The area directly behind your vehicle.,c:The view you see in your rearview mirror.
note: A blind spot is any area around your vehicle that you cannot see with your mirrors alone and must turn your head to check. Because mirrors do not show everything to the sides and rear, you must briefly look over your shoulder to see these hidden areas before changing lanes or merging.

question: How do worn or bald tires affect vehicle performance?
options: a:They can increase your stopping distance.,b:They can make turning more difficult.,c:They are likely to hydroplane.,d:All of the above.
note: Worn or bald tires are dangerous because they reduce traction. With less tread, your stopping distance increases, your ability to turn and corner safely is reduced, and your vehicle is more likely to hydroplane on wet roads. Good tread helps channel water away and grip the road, so tires should be replaced before they become bald.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who yields?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.
note: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions at intersections without traffic signals.

question: Where are you prohibited from parking?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On a hill.,c:Within 12 inches of the curb when on the street.,d:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: You may not park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane because these areas must stay clear for pedestrians and cyclists. When parking along a curb, you must be close to it—typically within about 12 inches—so your vehicle does not block traffic or create a hazard.

question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head to look over your shoulder into the blind spot.,b:Rely only on your inside rearview mirror.,c:Use only the outside mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, always turn your head and quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see into your blind spot, where mirrors cannot show vehicles that may be beside you.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They always have the right-of-way.,b:They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.,c:They are often harder to see in traffic.
note: Smaller road users like motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians are harder to see, especially in blind spots, at night, or in bad weather. Because they are less visible and more vulnerable in a crash, you must scan carefully and be extra alert for them.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left?
options: a:Glance over your left shoulder.,b:Check your right-side mirror.,c:Use only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; there is a blind spot to each side. Before changing lanes to the left, quickly glance over your left shoulder to check that blind spot and be sure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is hidden there.

question: What must you do if a bus is signaling to re-enter traffic after stopping to load or unload?
options: a:Yield and allow the bus to re-enter safely.,b:Honk to alert the bus driver.,c:Maintain speed and position.
note: When a bus signals to re-enter traffic after loading or unloading passengers, you should slow down or change lanes if needed and allow it to merge safely. Large buses need more time and space to pull out, and yielding helps protect boarding and exiting passengers.

question: Where must you keep proof of liability insurance while operating a vehicle?
options: a:In a safety deposit box at the bank.,b:In your vehicle whenever it is being operated.,c:At your place of employment.
note: Drivers are generally required to carry proof of liability insurance in the vehicle and present it to law enforcement when requested. Keeping it in the vehicle ensures you can show that the car is insured whenever it is being driven.

question: What should you adjust first when preparing to drive a vehicle?
options: a:Your seat position so you can see and reach controls.,b:Your rearview mirror only.,c:The steering wheel only.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can comfortably reach the pedals, steering wheel, and controls and have a clear view of the road. Once your seating position is correct, adjust your mirrors and steering wheel to match that position.

question: When a stopped school bus extends its stop arm and displays stop signals, drivers should:
options: a:Continue driving when they think most kids are done exiting.,b:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,c:Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped. Stay stopped until the bus starts moving again and the stop arm and flashing red lights are turned off. This protects children who may be crossing in front of or behind the bus.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Cause excessive oil use.,b:Require your vehicle to need tune-ups sooner.,c:Make you drowsy or expose you to toxic fumes.,d:Improve fuel efficiency.
note: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide and other toxic gases enter the passenger compartment. These fumes can make you drowsy, impair your judgment, or even be fatal. If you suspect an exhaust leak, have it inspected and repaired immediately and avoid driving with windows tightly closed until it is fixed.

question: What is distracted driving characterized as?
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Extremely risky behavior.,c:Nothing to be concerned about.
note: Distracted driving means your attention is not fully on the driving task. This includes using a phone, eating, adjusting controls, or anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving. It is extremely risky because it greatly increases your chance of not seeing hazards in time to react.

question: Which of the following types of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs,b:Only over-the-counter cold remedies,c:Prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can all impair driving.
note: Many substances can impair driving, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter remedies like some cold or allergy medicines. They can slow your reactions, affect your judgment, and make you drowsy. Always read labels and follow medical advice, and never drive if a drug makes you feel impaired.

question: How can you avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors more frequently.,c:Honk before changing lanes.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure the blind spot is clear. Use your mirrors and signals, but always include a head check to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red light is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A solid red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: Which combination provides the most protection in a crash?
options: a:An airbag only.,b:A lap and shoulder belt only.,c:A lap/shoulder belt used with an airbag.
note: The safest protection in a crash is a properly worn lap and shoulder belt used together with airbags. Seat belts keep you in position so the airbag can work correctly and reduce the risk of serious injury.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to make the intersection.,b:Prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Stop abruptly in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should prepare to stop and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely, rather than speeding up to beat the light.

question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, what is recommended?
options: a:Keep driving but do arm exercises every hour.,b:Drive with one eye closed to stay alert.,c:Stop and rest about every two hours.
note: On long trips, stop and rest about every two hours to reduce fatigue. Get out, stretch, and if you feel drowsy, pull off the road in a safe place and rest before continuing.

question: When crossing railroad tracks, what should you do to be safe?
options: a:Cross quickly when a train is approaching.,b:Only look both ways when the red light is flashing.,c:Turn on your headlights before crossing.,d:Look and listen both ways and only proceed when it is safe.
note: Before crossing railroad tracks, slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and watch for signals or gates. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: How is drinking and driving best described?
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem.,b:A minor traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving after drinking alcohol or using impairing drugs is a major cause of serious crashes, injuries, and deaths. Even small amounts of alcohol can slow reaction time, reduce coordination, and impair judgment, so it is always treated as a serious traffic safety problem.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.,b:The posted maximum speed only.,c:A speed that is slower than surrounding traffic regardless of conditions.
note: Speed limits are set for ideal conditions. By law, you must never drive faster than is safe and reasonable for current conditions such as rain, fog, traffic, or road surface, even if that means driving below the posted speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you need to make a turn but you are not in the proper lane, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Drive to the next intersection and then make the turn from the proper lane.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to turn safely, continue straight and turn at the next intersection. Sudden lane changes or cutting across traffic can cause crashes because other drivers are not expecting your movement.

question: When sharing the road with large trucks, remember that trucks generally:
options: a:Require less time to pass on a downgrade.,b:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.,c:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need more distance to slow down and stop. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them and allow extra space because they cannot stop as quickly as smaller vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle end up?
options: a:In the right lane of the one-way street.,b:In the center of the street.,c:In the left lane of the one-way street.,d:In any lane available.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the lane closest to you—the left lane of the one-way street. Turning into the nearest appropriate lane helps prevent conflicts with traffic in other lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should you begin slowing down when exiting a highway?
options: a:On the main road, just before the exit lane.,b:Once you have moved into the exit lane.,c:Once you see a toll booth.
note: On freeways and highways, you should maintain your speed on the main roadway and move into the exit (deceleration) lane at about the same speed as traffic. Once you are fully in the exit lane, then begin slowing to the posted exit or ramp speed. Slowing on the main road before entering the exit lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: Which of the following is true regarding sudden weather changes?
options: a:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in your driving.,b:You should not adjust your speed when it rains.,c:Be less aware of vehicles behind you in bad weather.,d:Weather does not affect stopping distance.
note: Sudden weather changes—such as rain, snow, fog, or strong wind—require you to adjust how you drive. You may need to slow down, increase your following distance, turn on headlights or wipers, and pay closer attention to traffic around you, including vehicles behind you. Bad weather usually increases stopping distance and reduces visibility, so you must drive more cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks.,b:Drivers must do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is careless.,c:Both A and B.
note: Drivers must use extreme care around pedestrians. You must always yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks and when they are legally crossing the street. Even if a pedestrian is crossing carelessly or outside a crosswalk, you must do everything you reasonably can to avoid hitting them, including slowing or stopping. However, pedestrians are also required to obey traffic signals and not suddenly step into the path of a vehicle.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers turned on.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches on a one-way street, you must pull over to the nearest edge or side of the roadway—right or left—clear of any intersection, and stop until it has passed. This gives the emergency vehicle a clear path and reduces the chance of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is a good general rule regarding passing other vehicles?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and safe.,b:Always pass on the right when possible.,c:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic quickly.
note: A safe general rule is to travel with the flow of traffic, staying within the speed limit, and pass only when it is both necessary and clearly safe. Passing always carries extra risk because it often requires moving into another lane or into oncoming traffic, so you should avoid unnecessary passing and never pass if you cannot complete the maneuver safely and legally.

question: What type of signs require drivers to obey the indicated instruction?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Regulatory signs are the signs you are legally required to obey. They include speed limit signs, stop and yield signs, and other signs that tell you what you must or must not do. Ignoring these signs can result in tickets or other penalties.

question: If you discover a vehicle defect that could affect safe operation, what should you do?
options: a:Have the defect corrected as soon as possible.,b:Drive slower and defer repair.,c:Correct it only when you can afford it.
note: If you find a defect that could affect safe operation—such as bad brakes, worn tires, or steering problems—you should not continue to drive as normal. The vehicle should be repaired as soon as possible, and you should avoid driving it until it is safe, or drive only the minimum necessary with extra caution to reach a repair facility.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The condition of the pavement.,d:All of the above.
note: Braking distance is affected by several factors: how fast you are going, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface. Higher speed, worn brakes or tires, and wet, icy, or loose pavement all increase the distance it takes to stop.

question: A “No stopping” sign means you may stop only under what circumstance?
options: a:Only to unload packages.,b:To avoid conflict with other traffic or to obey traffic control.,c:To discharge passengers whenever you wish.
note: A No Stopping sign means you may not stop your vehicle on that part of the road except when it is necessary to obey a traffic signal or officer, or to avoid a conflict with other traffic. You may not stop there to load or unload people or goods.

question: If your wheels slip off the paved road onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually, then steer back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,c:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the gas, and slow down gradually. Once you have reduced speed and it is safe, gently steer back onto the pavement. Sudden jerking of the wheel or hard braking can cause you to lose control.

question: When passing a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing on the roadway shoulder, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.,c:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes away from the stopped emergency vehicle.
note: Move over a lane if it is safe; otherwise, slow to a safe speed below the limit and give the stopped vehicle as much space as possible.

question: What does a solid white center line on a multi-lane roadway usually mean?
options: a:It separates lanes moving in the same direction and indicates lane changes are discouraged or may be prohibited.,b:It separates traffic moving in opposite directions.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may pass freely.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line between lanes means lane changes are discouraged and may be prohibited in some locations, such as near intersections or in tunnels. Drivers should generally stay in their lane and avoid crossing a solid white line unless necessary and legal.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a roadway indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,b:The line marks the edge of the roadway.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,d:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may pass when it is safe.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may change lanes or pass across a broken white line when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: What is the best way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Slow down and maintain tires in good condition while watching for standing water.,b:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed.,c:Drive faster to get across puddles quickly.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. To reduce the risk, slow down in wet conditions, keep your tires properly inflated and with good tread, and avoid driving through standing water or deep puddles whenever possible.

question: When must you pull over and allow an emergency vehicle to pass?
options: a:Only if it is following you.,b:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.,c:Regardless of its direction, pull to the right edge and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right as you safely can and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement. This applies whether it is coming from behind you, ahead of you, or from a side street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a \No standing\" sign allow you to do at that location?"
options: a:You may never stop your vehicle there.,b:You may stop temporarily only to pick up or discharge passengers.,c:You may park there if the driver remains in the vehicle.
note: A No Standing sign means you may stop only briefly to pick up or drop off passengers, but you may not wait, stand, or park there for any other reason. You also may not load or unload cargo. Parking is never allowed in a No Standing zone.

question: Which pavement marking or lane control device directs drivers into proper turn lanes?
options: a:Arrow pavement markings and lane arrows.,b:Flashing red lights.,c:White lines on the side of the road.
note: Arrow symbols painted on the pavement and lane-use arrows on signs show which lanes are for turning left, turning right, or going straight. Drivers must follow these arrows to be in the correct lane before reaching an intersection.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which of the following?
options: a:The effect that alcohol has.,b:The effect that amphetamines have.,c:The effect that anger has.
note: Driving while very tired can slow your reaction time, reduce your awareness, and impair judgment in ways similar to alcohol. After many hours awake, your driving performance can resemble that of a driver who is legally impaired by alcohol.

question: What is the key principle of speed management for curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve.,b:Maintain the posted speed through the curve then brake at the end.,c:Accelerate upon entering the curve.
note: You should reduce speed before entering a curve, then steer smoothly through it. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control because your tires are already working to change direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a Merging traffic sign on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed.,b:Make room for entering vehicles—move over a lane if safe.,c:Honk at incoming traffic.
note: When you see a Merging Traffic sign, be prepared for vehicles entering your lane. If possible, change lanes away from the merge area or adjust your speed to create a safe gap so merging drivers can enter smoothly.

question: Which type of sign warns drivers about potentially hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Information signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Warning signs are usually yellow with black symbols or words and are used to alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings. Recognizing and responding to these signs early helps you adjust speed and position to avoid crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What determines the space you need to cross traffic safely?
options: a:Road and weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:Presence of a stop sign only.,c:Whether you used your turn signal.
note: To cross traffic safely, you must have a large enough gap considering how fast other vehicles are coming, how far away they are, and how road and weather conditions affect your ability to accelerate and clear the intersection. Wet, icy, or uneven surfaces mean you need even more time and space to cross safely.

question: On a two-lane highway, when must you stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights?
options: a:If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.,b:When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.,c:When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
note: On a two-lane road with no physical divider, all traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, because children may be crossing the road from either side.

question: What color are guide (destination) signs?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:Yellow
note: Guide or destination signs that show directions, distances, and route information are typically green with white letters and symbols. These signs help you navigate to cities, exits, and major routes while driving.

question: What is the safest approach to driving on slick roads?
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Change lanes quickly.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual.
note: On slick roads, such as when it is raining, icy, or covered with wet leaves, you should slow down and take turns more gently than usual. Reducing speed and steering smoothly helps maintain traction and reduces the chance of skidding or losing control.

question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather regarding following distance?
options: a:Increase their speed to arrive sooner.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Increase their following distance.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or other bad weather, you need more space to react and stop because traction and visibility are reduced. Increasing your following distance gives you extra time to see hazards and brake smoothly, which helps prevent rear‑end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to pass another vehicle using the road shoulder?
options: a:Generally not permitted; only where specifically allowed by law and signs.,b:Sometimes allowed when the vehicle ahead is turning left and it is legal and safe.,c:Not allowed just to go around a slow-moving vehicle.
note: You must not drive on the shoulder to pass in normal situations because it is not a regular travel lane and other drivers and pedestrians do not expect vehicles there. However, some states allow limited shoulder use when the vehicle ahead is making a left turn and there is a paved shoulder on the right, if it can be done safely and is not prohibited by signs or markings. Always follow your state’s specific rules and markings before considering any shoulder use.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection has the same requirement as which sign?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A slow sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must treat the intersection like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, look for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe and after yielding the right‑of‑way as required.

question: A driver’s license may be suspended if the driver does what regarding a chemical test?
options: a:Drives 10 mph over the speed limit.,b:Honks a horn in a residential area after midnight.,c:Refuses to submit to a chemical test when requested.
note: Under implied consent laws, by driving you agree to take a chemical test (such as breath or blood) if lawfully requested. Refusing this test usually results in an automatic license suspension, even if you are not convicted of DUI.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, drivers should do which of the following?
options: a:Use only parking lights.,b:Use four-way flashers.,c:Keep vehicle lights off.,d:Turn on headlights.
note: At dusk, dawn, and on overcast days, turning on your headlights makes it easier for you to see and for others to see you. Use low beams when there is oncoming traffic or when you are following another vehicle closely so you do not blind other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Only when changing lanes.,b:Only when pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Whenever you change direction—changing lanes, parking, or entering traffic.
note: Turn signals must be used any time you change direction or move laterally in traffic—this includes changing lanes, turning, entering or leaving a parking space, and entering traffic from a driveway, alley, or parking lot—so other road users can anticipate your movement.

question: Which is true about drowsy drivers?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio will reliably keep them alert.,b:Drinking strong black coffee will always keep them safe to drive.,c:Drowsy drivers can operate so poorly that they may appear to be intoxicated.
note: Drowsy driving can slow reaction time, impair judgment, and cause lane drifting in ways very similar to alcohol impairment. Tricks like opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee are not reliable; the only safe solution is rest or changing drivers.

question: If a driver's left arm is extended downwards, what is that hand signal indicating?
options: a:Turning right.,b:Turning left.,c:Stopping or slowing.
note: Standard hand signals with the left arm are: straight out for a left turn, up for a right turn, and down for slowing or stopping. A left arm extended downward tells others you are slowing or stopping so they can adjust their speed and following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage, alley, or driveway.,b:Only when they are on a road to your left.,c:Only when you have a yield sign.
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway, alley, or garage, you must yield to all traffic already on the road and to pedestrians on any sidewalk you cross. Vehicles already on the main road have the right-of-way over vehicles entering from private drives or alleys.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted and driving with one hand while talking to a passenger, what is the safest response?
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space because their attention is reduced.,b:Follow exactly the same driving style.,c:Attempt to pass immediately.
note: When you notice another driver is distracted, increase your following distance and avoid driving alongside them. Extra space gives you more time to react if they drift, brake suddenly, or make an unexpected maneuver.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It prevents distractions from nearby vehicles.,b:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:It keeps traffic flowing faster.
note: Maintaining a space cushion means leaving enough room around your vehicle so you have time and space to react if another driver suddenly brakes, swerves, or if a hazard appears. This extra space helps you avoid sudden, unsafe maneuvers and reduces the chance of collisions.

question: To lessen the effects of headlight glare at night, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:At the center of the road.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: At night, bright headlights from oncoming traffic can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road ahead while still keeping track of your lane position. This helps protect your night vision while you continue to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working signals, you should:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the officer.,b:Obey the traffic lights instead of the officer.,c:Honk at the officer to get more information.,d:Wait for a written instruction.
note: When a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic, their hand signals and instructions override traffic lights and signs. You must follow the officer’s directions, even if the traffic signal shows a different indication, to keep traffic moving safely and avoid conflicts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are points on your driving record?
options: a:They are beneficial when applying for driving jobs.,b:Points are added to your driving record after convictions and can lead to loss of driving privileges.,c:They are nothing to worry about.
note: Points are added after traffic convictions; accumulating too many can result in license suspension or revocation.

question: Why must you be more cautious when driving at night?
options: a:There is a larger volume of traffic at night.,b:Traffic moves faster at night.,c:Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
note: At night, your ability to see is reduced, even with headlights, and it is harder to judge distances and spot hazards. Because drivers cannot see as well in the dark, you must slow down, increase following distance, and use headlights from about one half hour after sunset to one half hour before sunrise or whenever visibility is poor.

question: How do you officially indicate you want to be an organ donor on your license?
options: a:Discuss your decision with your next of kin only.,b:Have two witnesses sign the back of your license.,c:Complete the organ donor information on the back of your license when applying or renewing.
note: To officially indicate you want to be an organ donor, you must register through an official method, such as completing the donor section when you apply for or renew your license or registering through your state’s donor registry. Simply talking to family or having witnesses sign your license is not enough by itself, though you should still inform your family of your decision.

question: When passing a bicyclist, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.,b:Honk to alert the bicyclist that you are passing.,c:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can safely pass.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them as much space as you safely can. Many states require at least 3 feet of clearance. Do not honk in a way that could startle the rider, and never drive in the bicycle lane to pass; you should move into the regular traffic lane only when it is safe and legal.

question: The act of turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:Required only when reversing.,b:Unnecessary.,c:A bad driving habit.,d:A good driving habit.
note: Before changing lanes, you should always check your mirrors and then quickly turn your head to check your blind spot. This over-the-shoulder glance helps you see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that mirrors alone may not show, making it an essential safe‑driving habit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Stop before the sidewalk or edge of the roadway and yield to pedestrians and approaching vehicles before entering.,b:Honk to alert approaching traffic and then enter.,c:Drive slowly into the street and expect approaching vehicles to yield.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before the sidewalk or edge of the roadway and yield to pedestrians and all traffic on the main road. Drivers on the street have the right‑of‑way; you may only proceed when it is clear and safe, without relying on your horn or expecting others to yield.

question: After a school bus unloads children and its stop arm is extended, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed only after the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, watching carefully for children.,b:Watch for children walking along or crossing the road and proceed very cautiously once the bus’s red lights and stop arm are no longer activated.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the area after the bus’s signals turn off.
note: After a school bus has unloaded children and the red lights and stop arm are no longer activated, you may proceed, but you must do so very cautiously and watch carefully for children walking along or crossing the road. Children can be unpredictable, so even after the bus moves or the signals stop, you should drive slowly and be prepared to stop.

question: For a driver age 21 or older, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is illegal to drive at or above in Missouri?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older in Missouri, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. This is the standard per se limit in Missouri and most U.S. states for adult drivers.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition will not make your driving unsafe?
options: a:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,b:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.,c:Drive within your physical limitations.,d:All of the above.
note: To make sure your physical condition does not make your driving unsafe, you should do all of the following: stay physically fit and get regular checkups, understand how any medicines you take affect your alertness and coordination, and drive only within your physical limits. If you feel ill, tired, or affected by medication, delay driving or find another way to travel.

question: In which situations is it important to reduce speed?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads, intersections, railroad crossings, and when the road is wet or slippery.,b:Only when you see road signs advising you to slow down.,c:Only at night.
note: You should slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, and whenever the road is wet, icy, or otherwise slippery. Reduced speed gives you more time to react and a shorter stopping distance in hazardous conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already inside an intersection and the signal turns yellow, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Stop in the center of the intersection.,b:Continue carefully through the intersection.,c:Turn on hazard lights and back up.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have entered the intersection, continue through carefully. The yellow signal warns that the light is about to turn red; stopping in the middle of the intersection or backing up is unsafe and illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an uncontrolled intersection, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Slow down, check left-right-left, and yield to vehicles from the right as needed.,c:Always come to a full stop.,d:Only yield if another vehicle signals.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, slow down and be ready to stop. Look left, right, then left again, and yield as needed, especially to vehicles already in the intersection and to vehicles approaching from your right. Enter only when you are sure it is safe.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Signal your intention, check blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear before moving.,b:Check your blind spot after beginning the lane change.,c:Signal only after you have moved into the lane.
note: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Move only after you are sure the lane is clear and you have enough space.

question: If another car is about to hit you, what is the correct way to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Use your emergency lights.,c:Sound your horn.
note: When you think another driver may not see you and a collision could happen, use your horn to get their attention quickly. The horn is designed as an immediate warning device; waving or using emergency flashers is slower and less effective in an imminent hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, how should you indicate turns?
options: a:Use your horn.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Use hand signals to show your turns.
note: If your turn signals fail, you must use standard hand and arm signals to indicate left turns, right turns, and slowing or stopping. Continue using hand signals until your turn signals are repaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down but keep moving.,b:Come to a full stop and proceed when it is safe.,c:Continue without stopping.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is to:
options: a:Get some coffee and keep driving.,b:Open your windows and continue.,c:Stop driving and rest.,d:Turn up the radio and stay alert.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol—pull over in a safe place and rest rather than trying to push on.

question: What should you do when you approach an accident scene?
options: a:Do not stop unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.,b:Pull over and watch the scene.,c:Stop and get out to see what happened.
note: At an accident scene, keep driving unless you are directly involved or emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely assist. Stopping just to look creates additional hazards, can cause more crashes, and blocks emergency vehicles. Stay focused on the road and be alert for people or vehicles near the scene.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas and keep steering straight.,b:Immediately apply the brakes hard.,c:Gradually slow down and pull off the road when safe.,d:Both a and c
note: When a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and gently ease your foot off the accelerator. Do not slam on the brakes, because that can cause loss of control. Once the vehicle slows and you have it under control, gradually steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection without a traffic signal, if a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing, who must yield?
options: a:Whoever started moving last.,b:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,c:Whoever is slower.
note: At intersections without signals, drivers must yield to pedestrians who are crossing the street. Pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk have the right-of-way, and drivers must wait until the pedestrian has safely crossed before turning or proceeding.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Both yellow and white
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Seeing a yellow center line means oncoming traffic is on the other side of that line.

question: Which of the following can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Obeying posted speed limits.,c:Using proper turn signals.,d:All of the above
note: Allowing extra travel time, obeying speed limits, and using turn signals all help reduce stress and misunderstandings on the road. When you are not rushed, follow the rules, and clearly communicate your intentions, you are less likely to drive aggressively or trigger road rage in others.

question: On average, how many standard alcoholic drinks does the body process per hour?
options: a:Three drinks per hour.,b:One drink per hour.,c:Two drinks per hour.
note: The body typically metabolizes about one standard drink per hour. This is only an average; factors like body size, sex, food intake, and health can change how quickly alcohol is processed, so you can still be impaired even if you drink less than one drink per hour.

question: When parked facing uphill with a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels sharply away from the curb.,b:Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.,c:Keep the front wheels straight ahead.
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will move toward and rest against the curb, helping prevent the car from rolling into traffic.

question: In foggy conditions, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Hazard lights.,c:High beam headlights.
