note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams, and fog lights if equipped, help you see the road and help others see you without excessive glare.

question: What does the term \No zone\" refer to?"
options: a:A roadway with stereo volume restrictions.,b:Blind spots around a truck or bus.,c:A special reduced-speed zone.
note: The "No Zone" is the large blind spot area around commercial trucks and buses—along the sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front—where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Staying out of these areas whenever possible helps avoid collisions because the truck or bus driver may not know you are there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling from a curb required?
options: a:Only necessary if other traffic is present.,b:Required by law and a good habit.,c:Necessary only during the maneuver, not beforehand.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or moving laterally; signaling is both the law and good practice.

question: If you hear an emergency vehicle siren but cannot see it, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving until you see the vehicle.,b:Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.,c:Slow down and do not stop until you can locate it.
note: If you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, you should safely pull as far to the right as possible and stop. This lets you determine where the vehicle is coming from and keeps the lane clear in case it is approaching on your street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to enter a freeway from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter because freeway traffic must yield to you.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a large gap.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to signal, build up speed, and match the flow of traffic. You must yield to vehicles already on the freeway and merge only when it is safe and there is a sufficient gap.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim their high beams, where should you look?
options: a:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This reduces glare while still letting you track your lane position and stay safely on course.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do with the ignition?
options: a:Turn off the engine.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:Only to make a turn.,b:At any time to pass slower traffic.,c:During daytime hours only.
note: A solid yellow center line generally means no passing. You may cross a solid yellow line only when making a turn, such as into a driveway or side road, and only when it is safe and legal to do so. You may not cross it just to pass slower traffic.

question: If you are ordered to install an ignition interlock device (IID), who pays for installation and monthly inspections?
options: a:You must pay for installation and monthly maintenance costs.,b:The court pays for installation.,c:The arresting officer pays the fees.
note: When a court orders an ignition interlock device, the driver is normally responsible for paying the installation and ongoing monitoring or maintenance fees. These costs are part of the conditions for keeping or reinstating driving privileges after an impaired-driving offense.

question: What is a likely administrative consequence after a first-time DWI conviction?
options: a:An administrative license suspension, often around 90 days for a first offense (varies by state).,b:A $50 fine.,c:No penalty if it's your first offense.
note: A first-time DWI conviction leads to an administrative license suspension of 90 days; court penalties can be additional.

question: A flashing yellow arrow for left turns means:
options: a:You should merge into the lane in the arrow's direction.,b:You must come to a complete stop before turning.,c:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow means you have a permissive turn: you may turn left, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Your turn is not protected, so you must wait for a safe gap before turning.

question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Staring at objects off the roadway or daydreaming while driving.,b:Maintaining eye contact during a conversation with a passenger instead of watching the road.,c:Only watching the vehicle ahead and failing to scan mirrors or the surrounding traffic.
note: An inattentive driver is mentally or visually distracted from the driving task, such as daydreaming or staring at things off the roadway. Safe drivers keep their eyes moving, scan the road ahead, check mirrors, and avoid focusing only on one vehicle or object.

question: Which statement best describes the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:A circular green sign.,b:A rectangular red sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle mounted on the vehicle.
note: Slow-moving vehicles, such as farm equipment or certain construction vehicles, display a reflective orange triangle on the rear. This emblem warns other drivers that the vehicle usually travels at 25 mph or less, so they should be prepared to slow down and pass only when safe and legal.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Speed limits.,c:No passing zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are yellow and placed on the left side of the road to mark the beginning of a no passing zone. When you see this sign, you must not start or continue a pass in that area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Advisory speed signs attached to curves indicate:
options: a:They may be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.,b:Recommended speeds for safe travel in the curve under normal conditions.,c:They have a triangular shape.
note: Advisory speed signs on curves show the recommended maximum safe speed for that curve under normal, dry conditions. In rain, snow, or ice, you should drive even slower than the advisory speed to maintain control.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you need to stop quickly, what technique should you use?
options: a:Firmly pump the brakes to stop while retaining steering control.,b:Hold down the brake pedal so it locks up.,c:Tap the brakes lightly while steering.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should use a pumping or squeeze-release braking technique in an emergency stop. This helps prevent the wheels from locking so you can still steer while slowing the vehicle quickly.

question: When stopped in a line of traffic at a railroad crossing with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,b:You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.,c:There is enough space for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks without stopping.
note: Before you cross railroad tracks, always be sure there is enough room on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks. Never enter a crossing unless you can drive completely across without stopping on the rails.

question: If you must reduce speed on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the parking brake.,b:Firmly apply your brakes.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: On a slippery road, ease off the accelerator first so the vehicle slows gradually. If you need to slow more, brake gently to avoid skidding; hard or sudden braking can cause loss of control.

question: Where do you go to take the Missouri driver examination?
options: a:Any Missouri State Highway Patrol examination station.,b:Any Department of Transportation office.,c:Any Missouri contract office.
note: In Missouri, the written, vision, and driving tests are given by the Missouri State Highway Patrol at their examination stations. You may contact the Missouri State Highway Patrol or the Department of Revenue to find the nearest exam station, but the actual exams are not given at general DOT or contract offices.

question: Which action helps reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Replace tires with bad tread.,b:Do not speed when roads are wet.,c:Ignore tire air pressure.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. The most important way to reduce this risk is to slow down on wet roads. Good tire tread and proper air pressure also help, but speeding on wet pavement greatly increases the chance of hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic light warns that which light will soon appear?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A steady red light.,c:A steady green light.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. It warns you to prepare to stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely. You should not speed up to beat the red light.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:When it is safe to change lanes.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:At any time regardless of conditions.
note: Dashed (broken) white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line when you are changing lanes or merging, but only after checking traffic and making sure it is safe to move.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When anything makes driving conditions less than perfect.,b:Only when entering a highway.,c:Whenever you see a police car.,d:Never.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum under ideal conditions. You must slow down whenever weather, traffic, visibility, or road surface conditions are less than perfect. You can be cited for driving too fast for conditions even if you are below the posted speed limit.

question: Before changing lanes on a highway, you should:
options: a:Signal and immediately change lanes if mirrors look clear.,b:Honk before changing lanes to warn others.,c:Check only the rearview mirror and then change lanes.,d:Signal, check rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder into the blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal first, then check your rearview and side mirrors, and finally turn your head to quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that mirrors may miss and prevents cutting off other drivers.

question: If another person is injured in an accident, how should you handle them?
options: a:Move them away from the scene immediately.,b:Do not move them unnecessarily; keep them warm and provide first aid if trained.,c:Always leave injured persons where they are and walk away.
note: If someone is injured in a crash, do not move them unless there is immediate danger (like fire or risk of another collision). Moving an injured person can worsen neck or back injuries. Keep them warm, reassure them, and provide first aid only if you are trained, while someone calls 911.

question: When a transit bus is signaling to pull back into traffic after a stop, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to the bus so it can re-enter traffic.,b:Honking is required to alert the bus.,c:Remain in your lane and maintain speed.
note: When a transit bus signals to leave a stop and re-enter traffic, you should yield by slowing, changing lanes, or stopping if needed so the bus can merge safely. Large buses need more space and time to pull out, and yielding helps prevent side-swipe and rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When it is safe and does not interfere with traffic.
note: A single broken white or yellow line means you may cross it to pass or change lanes only when it is safe and will not interfere with other traffic. You must be sure you have enough space and visibility to complete the maneuver without forcing other drivers to slow or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far in advance should you signal before making a turn?
options: a:35 feet,b:50 feet,c:At least 100 feet before the turn.
note: On most roads, you must signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians have time to see your signal and react. At higher speeds, such as on highways, you should signal even earlier to give extra warning.

question: Which color line divides lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Red.,b:White.,c:Yellow.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and red is generally used for things like wrong-way or do-not-enter markers, not lane division.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers may pass when it is safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either direction. You may usually cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and not prohibited by signs.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wearing your seat belt.,b:Driving only on weekdays.,c:Staying in the right lane on multilane highways.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective way to reduce the risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Seat belts keep you from being thrown from the vehicle and help your body slow down more safely with the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against a red, you should:
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Honk your horn to hurry them.,c:Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.,d:Drive around them on the shoulder.
note: Even if you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk or intersection. Slow or stop as needed and allow them to cross safely before you proceed.

question: What is the maximum permitted tint (light blockage) for front door windows in Missouri?
options: a:Up to 65 percent light blockage is allowed on front door windows.,b:No tint is allowed on front door windows.,c:Any amount of tint is allowed as long as you can see out.
note: Missouri law allows front door windows to have tint that blocks up to 65% of light, meaning at least 35% of light must pass through. Darker tint than this on the front side windows can reduce visibility and is not legal.

question: Who benefits most from wearing seat belts?
options: a:All occupants of a vehicle, including the driver.,b:Only the driver.,c:Only passengers on long trips.
note: Seat belts protect everyone in the vehicle, not just the driver. In a crash, unbelted occupants can be thrown around inside the car or ejected, greatly increasing the risk of serious injury or death to themselves and others. The safest practice is for every person in the vehicle to wear a seat belt on every trip.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Look in your mirrors, check your blind spot over your shoulder, signal, and then change lanes when safe.,b:Sound your horn repeatedly before changing lanes.,c:Turn on your headlights before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, you must check your mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot, then signal and change lanes only when it is safe. The shoulder check helps you see vehicles that do not appear in your mirrors. Sounding your horn or turning on headlights is not a normal or sufficient method for checking if a lane is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a No right on red sign mean?
options: a:You may turn right on red if the way is clear.,b:You cannot turn right on red.,c:The intersection has a high number of traffic crashes.
note: A “No Right on Red” sign means you must remain stopped at the red light and may not turn right while the signal is red, even after coming to a complete stop. You must wait for a green light or a green arrow that allows the turn before proceeding.

question: How old must you be to obtain an instruction permit (young driver)?
options: a:15 years old.,b:14 years old.,c:15 and one-half years old.
note: In Missouri, a young driver can obtain an instruction permit at age 15. This permit allows supervised driving so the new driver can gain experience before being licensed to drive alone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:On a hill or curve where you cannot see far enough ahead.,b:When approaching or within an intersection.,c:When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended.
note: Passing is prohibited in several situations, including on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, when approaching or within an intersection, and when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. You must always stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and may not pass it until the lights stop flashing and it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic already on the roadway.,b:Blow your horn to warn vehicles you are entering.,c:Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all pedestrians and to vehicles already on the road. Do not pull out until you are sure it is safe and you will not force others to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: Before backing out of a driveway when children are nearby, you should:
options: a:Walk to the rear of the vehicle to be sure the way is clear.,b:Sound your horn to warn the children.,c:Rev the engine to warn them.,d:Rely only on mirrors while backing slowly.
note: Children can be too small to see in mirrors or cameras. Before backing when children may be nearby, walk to the rear of the vehicle and check the area directly behind and around it, then back slowly while continuing to check mirrors and surroundings.

question: On a highway with double solid yellow center lines, when is crossing allowed?
options: a:Cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross to pass slow vehicles when safe.,c:Never cross under any circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow center lines mean no passing in either direction. You may not cross them to pass, but you may carefully cross them to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or private road when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: How should you handle driving near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Take the right-of-way immediately.,c:Proceed normally without changing speed.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have the right-of-way. Slow down well in advance, be prepared to stop, and allow them to cross safely without rushing or startling them.

question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the vehicle in front of the parking space.,b:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.,c:Turn your wheels to the right immediately.
note: To begin parallel parking, first signal, check traffic, and pull up so your vehicle is parallel and even with the vehicle in front of the space. From this position you can then turn the wheel and back into the space under better control.

question: Vehicle stopping distances depend on many factors. Which of the following NEVER affects stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance is made up of reaction distance and braking distance. Your reaction time, vehicle speed, brake and tire condition, road surface, and visibility all affect how long it takes to stop. The time of day by itself does not change stopping distance, although conditions that often occur at night (like fatigue or poor visibility) can.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:Only when driving in rural areas.,d:Whenever there is a police car nearby.
note: You must adjust your speed to traffic, road, and weather conditions, even if that means driving below the posted limit. However, it is illegal to drive so slowly that you unnecessarily block or interfere with the normal, reasonable flow of traffic, unless you are doing so for safety or as required by law.

question: Anything that requires you to which of the following could cause a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road.,b:Take your hands off the wheel.,c:Take your attention away from the task of driving.,d:Any of the above.
note: Any distraction that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving can lead to a crash. Looking away, reaching for objects, or thinking about something other than driving all reduce your ability to react quickly to hazards.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should you drive?
options: a:Sound your horn whenever you see children.,b:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,c:Always stop whether a stop sign is posted or not.
note: Near school crossings you must slow down, watch carefully for children who may enter the road unexpectedly, and be prepared to stop. Always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and obey any reduced school-zone speed limits or crossing guard instructions.

question: What headlights should you use when driving in rain?
options: a:Use low beam headlights.,b:Use high beam headlights.,c:Use only parking lights.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, use low beam headlights. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road while making your vehicle more visible to others. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder for you and other drivers to see.

question: If sleet or snow begins while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Approach all vehicles with caution.,b:Allow extra space between your vehicle and vehicles ahead.,c:Keep windshield and mirrors clear.
note: In sleet or snow, your stopping distance increases because the road is slippery. You should slow down and leave extra space between your vehicle and the one ahead so you have more time and distance to react and stop safely.

question: Which is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Never place a rear-facing infant in the front seat of a vehicle with an active passenger airbag.,b:An airbag by itself is always safer than a seat belt.,c:Infants may be held safely by a strong adult during travel.
note: A rear-facing infant seat must never be placed in front of an active passenger airbag because the airbag can strike the back of the seat and seriously injure or kill the infant. Children should be properly restrained in appropriate child seats, usually in the rear seat.

question: What should you do before switching on the ignition?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers are buckled.,b:Make sure only adult passengers have fastened belts.,c:Buckle only the driver and child passengers.
note: Before starting the vehicle, the driver should buckle their own safety belt and make sure every passenger is properly restrained. This habit ensures everyone is protected from the moment the vehicle begins moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you arrive at the same time as a vehicle on your right, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Speed up to get through first.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed when safe.,c:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. Wait until it is safe and clear, then proceed through the intersection.

question: Why is night driving generally more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:It is more likely to rain at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,c:Cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: Driving at night is harder because you cannot see as far or as clearly as in daylight. Reduced visibility means you must rely on headlights and should drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a freeway, if you miss your exit what should you do?
options: a:Make the exit quickly from your current lane.,b:Stop and back up on the shoulder.,c:Continue to the next exit and re-route safely.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit. Stopping, backing up, or cutting across lanes or the median is extremely dangerous and illegal on freeways. After exiting at the next opportunity, find a safe route to get back to your intended destination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If your slow speed is causing a line of vehicles to form behind you, you should safely pull off to the right when possible and let them pass. This is especially important on two-lane roads where passing opportunities are limited. Blocking faster traffic can increase driver frustration and lead to unsafe passing maneuvers.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,b:You are moving faster than the bicycle and the cyclist is vulnerable to serious injury.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.
note: You must be cautious when passing a bicycle because you are moving much faster and a small mistake can seriously injure the cyclist. Give them plenty of space, slow down if needed, and only pass when it is safe and legal. Oncoming traffic is a concern, but the primary safety issue is your higher speed and the cyclist’s vulnerability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady green arrow at an intersection means drivers may:
options: a:Always stop before turning.,b:Turn without yielding to anyone.,c:Ignore the arrow and proceed straight only.,d:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A steady green arrow means you may make the turn in the direction of the arrow. This is a protected turn, but you must still yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection and complete the turn carefully. Do not proceed straight if the signal only shows a green arrow for turning.

question: What does a solid red arrow displayed by a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Stop; you may not turn in the direction indicated until a green signal appears.,b:Proceed with caution and turn when safe.,c:It has no meaning and should be ignored.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to turn in the direction of the arrow. You must remain stopped until the signal changes to a green arrow or a green light that permits the movement, and then proceed only when it is safe and legal.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Maintain the same speed and block the pass.,c:Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle so they can pass safely.
note: If another driver wants to pass you, you should help them do it safely. Keep a steady path and gently slow down to create more space in front of you. This gives the passing driver more room and time to move back into the lane without cutting too closely in front of you.

question: Which of the following is NOT true about winter driving?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter conditions is safe.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important.
note: You should not use cruise control on snow, ice, or in other slippery winter conditions because it can cause you to lose control if the vehicle starts to skid. Winter is generally the most difficult driving season due to ice, snow, and reduced visibility, and checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important to keep the vehicle running safely and to maintain a clear windshield.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the wheel firmly and steer straight while easing off the gas, then brake gently when under control.,b:Brake hard immediately.,c:Maintain speed and keep steering steady until you reach a pullover spot.
note: When a tire blows out, the sudden loss of air can pull the vehicle to one side. Grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight, then gently ease off the accelerator. Do not brake hard right away, because that can cause a skid or loss of control. Once the vehicle is stable and slowing, brake gently and move off the road to a safe place.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes you.,b:Drive with your flashers on.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle approaching from behind, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed. This creates a clear path so they can respond quickly and safely to emergencies.

question: What color are highway destination (exit/distance) signs?
options: a:Red with white letters.,b:Yellow with black letters.,c:Green with white letters.
note: Highway guide signs that show destinations, exits, and distances use a green background with white letters or symbols. These signs help drivers navigate to cities, streets, and highway routes and are different from warning signs (yellow) and regulatory signs like stop or yield (red or white).

question: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, what precautions should you take?
options: a:Sit in your car and wait for help with hazards off.,b:Signal, move completely off the road if possible, turn on four-way flashers, and raise the hood.,c:Sound your horn at passing motorists.
note: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, you should get as far off the roadway as possible, turn on your hazard (four‑way) flashers, and raise the hood or use other signals so other drivers can see that your vehicle is disabled. This reduces the risk of being hit by passing traffic and helps emergency or roadside assistance locate you.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Overcorrect.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is generally the same direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding. This helps you straighten the car and regain control. Avoid jerking the wheel or overcorrecting, as that can cause a spin or send you into another lane.

question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, how should you respond?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.,b:Slow down and move to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, then stop if necessary.,c:Stop as quickly as possible in your lane.
note: On a divided multilane highway, when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by slowing down and moving as far to the right as you safely can to create a clear path. Stop if necessary and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed. Never ignore the emergency vehicle or block its route.

question: If you become stranded during a snowstorm, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Get out of the car and walk for help.,b:Lay down in your car and go to sleep.,c:Stay in your vehicle and wait for help while conserving heat.
note: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, it is usually safest to stay with your vehicle. The vehicle provides shelter, makes you easier to find, and protects you from getting lost or exposed to severe cold. Run the engine only periodically to conserve fuel and reduce the risk of carbon monoxide poisoning, and keep the exhaust pipe clear of snow.

question: What does a single broken yellow centerline indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
note: A single broken yellow centerline means traffic in the two lanes moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it can be done safely. You may cross the line to pass another vehicle, but only when you have enough clear distance ahead and no oncoming traffic or other hazards.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you set your steering?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,c:Keep rear tires against the curb.
note: When you park uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will move toward and rest against the curb, helping stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: How should a seat belt fit when properly adjusted?
options: a:Loose across the waist.,b:Buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,c:Hidden beneath the seat for comfort.
note: A properly adjusted seat belt fits snugly, not loosely. The lap belt should rest low across your hip bones and lower abdomen, and the shoulder belt should cross the center of your chest and shoulder. This positioning helps the strongest parts of your body absorb crash forces and reduces the risk of internal injuries.

question: In Missouri, an adult (21+) is prohibited from driving with a minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.08 percent
note: For drivers 21 and older in Missouri, it is illegal to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. This 0.08% limit is the standard per se impairment level used in most U.S. states for adult drivers.

question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to:
options: a:Vehicles and bicyclists already in the roundabout and pedestrians at crosswalks.,b:Only pedestrians in the roundabout.,c:None; proceed immediately.
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to traffic and bicyclists already circulating in the roundabout, as well as pedestrians in crosswalks at the entrances and exits. Enter only when there is a safe gap in traffic.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you glance to avoid glare?
options: a:Look toward the center of the road.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look toward either side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the glare. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road while still keeping track of your lane position. This reduces glare and helps you stay safely in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must stop at an intersection and there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see traffic without entering it.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:Where you can see at least 200 feet in both directions even if you must enter the intersecting road.
note: When there is no stop line or crosswalk, you must still stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic, but without moving into the cross traffic lane.

question: When are roads especially slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:Only after it has been raining for an hour.,b:Only when temperatures are below freezing.,c:The day after it rains.,d:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
note: Roads are most slippery at the beginning of a rainstorm, usually the first 10–15 minutes. Oil and residue on the road mix with the water and rise to the surface, reducing traction until the rain washes them away.

question: Which of the following are effects alcohol can have on you?
options: a:It impairs your thinking ability.,b:It gives you a feeling of false confidence.,c:It slows your reaction time.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol affects many parts of driving performance. It impairs your thinking and judgment, slows your reaction time, and can give you a false sense of confidence. Any of these effects can make you unsafe to drive.

question: If the center of the road has a broken yellow line, what does that indicate?
options: a:Traffic flows in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:No passing is allowed.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed on your side when it is safe and legal. You must still check for oncoming traffic and ensure you have enough space to pass.

question: How does alcohol affect driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgement.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It has no effect on either.
note: Alcohol reduces your ability to control the vehicle and make good decisions. It slows reactions, affects coordination and vision, and weakens judgment, so it harms both driving skills and judgment.

question: What is the purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:They indicate what a driver must or must not do.,b:They mark places of present danger.,c:They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
note: Regulatory signs tell you the traffic laws and rules you must follow in that specific area, such as speed limits, stop or yield requirements, lane use, and parking restrictions. They indicate what you must or must not do, and you are legally required to obey them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left but oncoming traffic is heavy while the light is green, what may you do to prepare for the turn?
options: a:Use the next intersection to turn.,b:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear and don’t enter the intersection.,c:Enter and wait in the center of the intersection when the light is green so you can complete the turn when safe.
note: When you have a green light and want to turn left, you may move into the intersection and wait with your wheels straight until there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic. When the way is clear—or when the light turns yellow or red and oncoming traffic stops—you complete the turn if it is safe. Do not wait behind the crosswalk if you intend to turn and it is legal to enter the intersection.

question: What do round traffic signs typically warn drivers about?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Upcoming railroad crossings.
note: Round traffic signs in the United States are used specifically to warn of an upcoming railroad crossing. When you see a round railroad warning sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicate?
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you are not allowed to pass other vehicles from your direction. It is used where passing would be unsafe, such as on hills, curves, or areas with limited visibility.

question: What is one danger of a leaky exhaust system?
options: a:It can lead to carbon monoxide entering the vehicle.,b:It decreases fuel economy.,c:It makes the engine quieter.
note: A leaky exhaust system can allow carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless poisonous gas, to enter the passenger compartment. Breathing carbon monoxide can cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, or death, so exhaust leaks must be repaired immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Ignore it and proceed at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You are expected to stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution rather than braking hard and risking a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn or changing lanes, what is required of drivers?
options: a:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,b:Signal only at night.,c:Always signal your intentions.
note: You must always signal when turning, changing lanes, entering or leaving a roadway, or pulling away from a curb, regardless of whether you see other traffic. Signaling every time lets other road users predict your actions and helps prevent crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Get out of the vehicle immediately.,b:Unbuckle and walk toward the officer.,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,d:Reach for your license and registration before the officer reaches you.
note: If stopped by police, stay in your vehicle unless the officer instructs otherwise. Keep your hands visible, usually on the steering wheel, and wait for the officer to approach and give directions. Only reach for your license, registration, or other documents after the officer asks you to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a flashing red traffic light, you must:
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed only when safe.,b:Slow down and continue without stopping.,c:Yield to traffic on the left only.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when traffic and pedestrians are clear and it is safe.

question: Which of the following does NOT influence Blood Alcohol Content (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much you drink.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink does not matter; only the total amount of alcohol you consume affects BAC.
note: Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) is affected by how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink, and your body weight, among other factors. A larger person will generally have a lower BAC than a smaller person who drinks the same amount in the same time. The type of alcoholic beverage matters only because different drinks contain different amounts of alcohol per serving; what ultimately affects BAC is the total amount of alcohol consumed, not whether it came from beer, wine, or liquor.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving, excessive speed for conditions, and following too closely.,b:Only bad weather.,c:Strictly vehicle defects.
note: Crashes are most often caused by driver behavior, not just weather or vehicle problems. Inattentive driving, driving too fast for road or traffic conditions, and following other vehicles too closely all reduce the time and space you have to react, which greatly increases the chance of a collision.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, what effects occur?
options: a:Your reaction time improves.,b:It speeds up alcohol metabolism.,c:Your reactions slow down and you become more confident.
note: As alcohol builds up in the bloodstream, it slows your brain and body. Your reaction time gets slower, your judgment and coordination get worse, and you may feel more confident or willing to take risks. This combination makes driving far more dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow arrow indicate?
options: a:Prepare to stop; a red arrow is about to appear.,b:You may turn left after yielding.,c:You should accelerate to clear the intersection.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turn phase is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should prepare to stop and must stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. Do not speed up to beat the red.

question: Which of the following is not a factor in determining how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.,d:Perception time.
note: Total stopping distance is made up of perception time (seeing the hazard), reaction distance (moving your foot to the brake), and braking distance (the distance the car travels after you apply the brakes). Steering ability does not change how far it takes the vehicle to come to a complete stop.

question: How does consuming alcohol affect a person who then drives?
options: a:Alcohol makes drivers better because they are more careful.,b:Alcohol impairs control over body and mind and reduces ability to operate a vehicle.,c:Drivers are always aware of the risks they are taking.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the central nervous system. It reduces judgment, coordination, vision, and reaction time, so drivers cannot control the vehicle as well or respond quickly to hazards, greatly increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.,b:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), the general rule is that the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This helps prevent confusion and collisions when vehicles arrive at the same time.

question: When driving near heavy trucks you and other highway users must allow for what?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Large trucks and other heavy vehicles need more distance to stop because of their size and weight. When driving near them, leave extra space in front of and behind them and avoid cutting in front of them so they have enough room to brake safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Other drivers already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic.,c:Pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: When making a left turn, you must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming traffic, to pedestrians in the crosswalk, and to any vehicles already in the intersection. Do not start your turn until the way is clear of oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and drive safely.,b:It decreases the chance of an accident.,c:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Stress, anger, or strong emotions can distract you, narrow your attention, and impair judgment. This makes it harder to notice hazards and react safely, increasing your risk of a crash. Calm down before driving and stay focused on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A solid yellow light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, watching carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians. Be prepared to stop if needed, but you are not required to stop if the way is clear.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions due to road work.,b:It is summer.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.
note: Work zone signs are orange and warn that road work or workers are present. They alert you that road or traffic conditions may be changed or less predictable, so you must slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for lane shifts, reduced speeds, or stopped traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Always come to a complete stop, then proceed in turn, giving the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right when arrival is simultaneous.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Passing is prohibited.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is dashed on your side and the way is clear, you may cross it to pass another vehicle, turn left, or enter/exit the roadway, but only when it is safe and legal.

question: If you see an animal in the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.,b:Honk repeatedly to move the animal quickly.,c:Pass as closely as possible to avoid delays.
note: When you see an animal in or near the roadway, slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass very cautiously. Give the animal plenty of space and avoid sudden movements or loud horn use that could startle it into your path.

question: Guide or destination signs are what color?
options: a:Green,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Guide and destination signs, such as those showing exits, routes, and distances, are typically green with white letters and symbols. They help you navigate by providing directional and location information.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow and stop if you can do so safely; otherwise proceed through the intersection.,b:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,c:Continue as if you have the right-of-way.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before the intersection. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through carefully rather than braking hard in the intersection.

question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping on:
options: a:A downhill grade.,b:At night.,c:A paved highway in good condition.,d:A wet or icy road.
note: Stopping distance increases whenever gravity, speed, or poor traction make it harder to slow down. On a downhill grade, gravity pulls your vehicle forward, so it takes more distance to stop than on level ground. Wet or icy roads also increase stopping distance, but among these choices, a downhill grade is the most directly correct and commonly tested factor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when changing lanes.,b:When pulling into or out of a parking space and when changing lanes.,c:Only when pulling into traffic from an alley.
note: You must signal any time you turn, change lanes, enter or leave a parking space, or pull into traffic from a curb, driveway, alley, or parking area. Signaling lets other road users know what you plan to do so they can react safely.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the best response?
options: a:Flash your lights to show you are right.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Call the police immediately from the roadway.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, focus on safety, not on being right. Stay calm, slow down if needed, and create space by letting them go ahead. Avoid eye contact, gestures, or actions that could escalate the situation.

question: What is a \No zone\" around a large vehicle?"
options: a:A one-way traffic area.,b:The blind spot areas around large trucks and buses.,c:A designated no passing zone.
note: A “No-Zone” is the large blind-spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you drive in these areas, the truck or bus driver may not know you are there, increasing the risk of a collision. Avoid lingering in these blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:A suggested safe speed regardless of conditions.,c:The speed you must drive even in dangerous conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed allowed only under ideal conditions. If weather, traffic, or road conditions are poor, you must drive slower than the posted limit so you can stop safely and maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill where a curb is present, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping prevent it from rolling into traffic.

question: What should be your first response when visibility decreases?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: When visibility decreases, you should immediately turn on your headlights so you can see better and be seen by others. Then adjust your speed to match how far you can see ahead, slowing down as needed to maintain a safe stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Treat it like a stop sign and stop.,c:Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any pedestrians or vehicles in or approaching the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your emergency flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or traffic striking your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.

question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only your rearview mirror.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors so you can choose a safe gap and merge smoothly.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn while being prepared to stop.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Continue at the same speed.
note: If a child appears ready to run into the street, immediately cover the brake and be prepared to stop while giving a sharp blast of your horn to warn the child and others nearby. Use the horn to alert, but your primary responsibility is to slow or stop to avoid a collision.

question: What must you do when approaching a pedestrian who uses a guide dog or white cane?
options: a:Honk so they know to clear the way.,b:Swerve quickly around them.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Stop and give the blind pedestrian the right-of-way; do not honk or attempt to steer around them abruptly.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of substance?
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:An antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity and impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making it dangerous to drive after drinking.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect which abilities?
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and physical coordination, even if you do not feel drunk. Because driving requires quick decisions and precise control, even small amounts of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

question: When is using your horn appropriate?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When another driver makes a mistake.,c:When another vehicle is in your way and you want them to move.
note: Use your horn only to alert others to a potential collision or to warn of immediate danger. Do not use it to show anger, impatience, or to punish other drivers for mistakes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Where signs and pavement markings indicate passing is permitted and it is safe.,b:Within an intersection if no oncoming vehicles are present.,c:On a curve if you can see ahead a short distance.,d:Anywhere if you signal before passing.
note: Passing is only safe and legal where signs and pavement markings allow it and you have enough clear space to pass without speeding or cutting back in too closely. Never pass in intersections, on curves, or where your view is blocked by hills or other obstacles.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to you.,b:You must yield to pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must yield to you.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether marked or unmarked, when pedestrians are in or approaching your lane. Always be prepared to stop for people crossing the street.

question: What does a green arrow signal require you to do?
options: a:Proceed immediately without yielding.,b:Ignore any pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,d:Yield to vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the intersection, then complete the turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected movement in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in the intersection before you complete your turn.

question: Why is winter driving more hazardous than other seasons?
options: a:There are increased hours of darkness.,b:Road conditions can be affected by freezing temperatures, ice, snow, and fog.,c:Both of the above.
note: Winter driving is more dangerous because there are more hours of darkness and road surfaces can become slippery or obscured by ice, snow, and fog. These conditions reduce traction and visibility, requiring slower speeds and greater following distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What general attitude should a driver have about right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Right-of-way laws say who should go first, but they do not guarantee that others will follow them. Safe drivers always stay ready to yield, even when they legally have the right-of-way, if yielding will prevent a collision.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, scan carefully for children, and be prepared to stop if they are in or near the crosswalk. You do not automatically stop unless required by a stop sign, signal, or pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: If a tire blows out suddenly while you're driving, what steps should you take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and exit the traffic lane slowly.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to stop quickly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge.,d:Turn on your hazards and speed up to reach the shoulder faster.
note: When a tire blows out, the car may pull to one side. Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down. Once it is under control and speed has dropped, steer gradually off the road and brake gently if needed. Sudden hard braking or sharp steering can cause loss of control.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:One,b:Two,c:Three
note: Alcohol begins to affect judgment and reaction time with the first drink. Even one drink can impair your ability to drive safely, so the safest choice is not to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Once alcohol is in your system, only time allows your body to metabolize it and lower your BAC. Food, coffee, cold showers, or exercise may make you feel more awake but do not speed up the elimination of alcohol.

question: When ridden on public roadways, bicycles are legally classified as:
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Vehicles.,c:Hazards.,d:Motor vehicles.
note: Bicycles ridden on public roads are treated as vehicles. Cyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules just like drivers of cars, including stopping at red lights and stop signs and riding in the same direction as traffic.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the lap belt.
note: If your vehicle has both a lap belt and a shoulder belt, you must wear both. The lap belt should be low and snug across the hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the chest and shoulder, not the neck or under the arm. Using only one part greatly reduces protection in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: You must not make a U‑turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure it is safe. Limited visibility makes it hard to judge oncoming traffic and can lead to serious head‑on collisions.

question: Driving noticeably slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad, but you must not drive so slowly that you unnecessarily block or endanger other traffic.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because other drivers may not expect it and may make sudden or risky lane changes or passing maneuvers. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic (within the speed limit) and adjust your speed reasonably for conditions, such as bad weather, without becoming an unnecessary obstruction.

question: What qualifies as a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from the driving task—your eyes from the road, your mind from driving, or your hands from the wheel. Examples include texting, eating, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers instead of traffic.

question: When following another vehicle at night, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle at night so you do not shine bright light into the driver’s mirrors and eyes. High beams can blind or distract the driver ahead, increasing the risk of a crash.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Neither lane may pass.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you want to change lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in an intersection because traffic movements are more complex and other drivers may not expect a lane change there. Instead, change lanes before or after the intersection, and always check mirrors, blind spots, and signal first.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what should you do to re-enter safely?
options: a:Wait until it is safe to do so, then gradually re-enter the roadway.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and keep a firm grip on the wheel. When traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement at a shallow angle. Do not jerk the wheel or brake hard, as that can cause you to lose control.

question: Which headlights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or sleet, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help other drivers see you without excessive glare.
